title: UPDATE! Amount of Hair Back!
text:
UPDATE! The Shrinking Packages of hair

BEFORE
In my last review, I commented that at the beginning, I was pleased with the price and that the amount of hair matched the pictures. Over time however, I found that:
1) the packaging changed from “factory original “ (like the clear plastic sleeves like you see braids come in) to ziplock bags (like you put your kid’s lunch in). Not cool, but not bad.
2) After the packaging change, I started to notice that each time I bought the hair, there was less and less hair in the little ziplock baggies. Definitely NOT cool and super BAD :-/

NOW!!!
Flyteng responded my review by suggesting I give them another try (no extra hair or admission of the skimping however). I did because the price was still great at a bit over 15 bucks and my hair did look really cute (for a little while at least- more later).

For the last three purchases, there has been more hair in the bags. V. Cool. Still in ziplocks though. Ratchet. The price has gone up close to 3 bucks, but at least the the amounts of hair are more consistent.

The Hair
It looks beautiful and natural for about a week. It’s soft and feels light and great. Something happens into the second week however and the hair starts to get hard and really nappy. Now full disclosure: when I install, I pull a lot of the coils apart. When I do this, it looks absolutely natural (I joined a Black Girl Magic Meet up - they ALL that it was mine and you know we know). Since I don’t mind nappy hair, it’s cool. I do have to cut the matted ends daily to not look like I haven’t been lost in the desert for a month, but again, I’m cool with that.

All in all, I would say that I will continue to use it as long as:
1) the price doesn’t continue to go up (might have to do with China tariffs - anybody else feeling this our hair products?).
2) they don’t start back skimping on the hair.

Happy Crocheting Y’all!!
Miss Bliss

title: Love and Hate this Scrub
text:
I have a bit of a love/hate relationship with this scrub. What I LOVE about it is the delicious, robust coffee scent. It is STRONG and packs a powerful punch in the morning, which helps to wake me up. I also love the serious grit it has to it. The texture varies from fine grounds to courser grounds, with a higher ratio of course grounds. Each scrub feels like it's getting deep into my skin. I feel like I'm scrubbing off layers of dead skin, dirt, grime, etc. when I'm using this. My skin feels smoother and softer after I use this scrub. I apply lotion straight out of the shower and my body is soft as a cloud!

What I sort of hate about this product is how messy it is. It just falls apart and gets everywhere. I included photos of what a hot mess my sink and shower look like after using it. Other scrubs I've used in the past have some agent that keeps them together to prevent it from going everywhere, but this doesn't. One I tried recently that I loved was JOON X MOON (https://www.amazon.com/Watermelon-Exfoliating-Moisturizing-Nourish-Essential/dp/B0876GX6MQ/ref=sr_1_2?dchild=1&keywords=moon+cube+body+scrub&qid=1600826357&sr=8-2), and that is in cube form to start, then breaks down to scrub as you rub it and use water. It does an incredible job of exfoliating without making a mess of my small shower. If you're not into the cube thing, I also like stuff that B&BW makes and they sell it on Amazon. It's has a paste-like consistency and does a good job at making your skin feel soft like a baby! Here is a Bath & Body Works aromatherapy scrub - I loooove this one: https://www.amazon.com/Bath-Body-Works-AROMATHERAPY-Eucalyptus/dp/B005LZUP36/ref=sr_1_14?dchild=1&keywords=sugar+scrub&qid=1600826921&sr=8-14

The other thing I wasn't a huge fan of was the packaging. I have a tiny shower, so it is impossible to take anything in there without getting wet. Every time I take this into the shower, I'm nervous the bag will get soaked and ruin it. There is a waxy coat applied to the bag, which helps protect it, but it still doesn't give me as much confidence as something like a glass jar or tin would. Ideally, the scrub wouldn't get soaked until I'm ready to use it. It has held up through 3 uses so far but I may transfer it into a mason jar and store it that way.

The other thing that really bummed me out was that is stained my clothes!!! I towel dried after shower, put on moisturizer, then light gray leggings. There must have been a tiny amount of residule coffee scrub because it stained my leggings!!

Overall, a decent scrub to try. Not my favorite scrub, since it stained my clothes and made my shower a mess.

title: Nice SPF for your Face (with safe ingredients).
text:
I have photosensitivity, so I use a lot of sunscreen. Because of that I have looked into safe brands. Badger is my favorite. However, I had been using their regular sunscreens on my body as well as my face, and realized maybe I should try this one that is specifically for the face. I'm glad I did.

Zinc oxide is a safe sun screen ingredient. The downside is that it can leave a white-ish residue on your skin. I found with Badger's (and all brands using zinc oxide) this was true. I am very pale so it's not a huge issue to me. And I solved it best by exfoliating my face a few times a week (the white tint seems to grab more onto dry patches) and also after putting on the sun screen, I use that mineral powder makeup and I just tap on a little of that to get my regular looking skin color back. But with the regular badger sun screens, like most with zinc oxide, you really have to rub it into your skin. It sort of starts to "melt" a bit and smooth out, and on my body it's no big deal. But on my face, with sensitive skin, I like to rub it as little as possible.

And that is where this facial sun screen lotion comes in perfect. It is easier to smooth onto your face. It is creamier and lighter in texture. There is a slight white-ish hue, especuially if you overdue it, but it seems less than when using the other bigger tubes of Badger sunscreen. And it feels nice on my skin and leaves if feeling soft afterwards.

This is my first bottle of this lotion and I find the rose scent to be faint. I smell it just slightly, sort of mixed with a slight clean, herbal sort of scent. And it fades away soon enough. I saw other reviews state the rose smell was too heavy or smelt like a grandmother, so I am not sure who's bottle is the norm, or who got a bottle that is unusual. I hope I didn't get an old bottle. But it seems to be working as far as sun protection. i would love if it smelled a bit more like rose because I love roses and their scent. It is real rose. Badger does not use fake fragrance.

This is now what I will be using on my face year long. (Unless they come out with a facial lotion with SPF 30, which would be great.)

title: This is NOT teal and it fades insanely quickly... fail 🥱👎🏼
text:
I was really excited about getting this hair dye and using it but sadly it was a GIGANTIC disappointment 😭

1.) On the bottle, in the item description, etc it says that the color lasts for 45 washes but I can promise you that it does NOT last that long heck it barely even lasted 10% as long as it claims to (and yes that's even with me only washing my hair in cold water, only washing my hair once a week, using color protecting products, etc). Within only 4 washes the color has drastically faded and there's even some spots where the color has completely washed out already leaving bleach blonde patches. There's a few semi/demi hair dyes i've used that will still stay pretty even when fading but unfortunately this isn't one of them- it's not ugly per say but it's really bland, lifeless and has me wanting to rush to the store to buy some more hair dye so I can fix it ASAP. I never thought in a million years i'd ever find a semi/demi hair dye that was worse then Splat when it came to fading but man this dye takes the cake- with me taking care of my colored hair properly Splat will last me 10 washes before it gets to the "ew ugly it faded I need to do a touch up" stage whereas once again this only lasted 4 washes.

2.) This color isn't teal in fact it's more of a dark blue with teal highlights/shine that you can only see if you're outside or standing directly under a light inside. I bleached my hair beforehand getting it 100% bleach blonde because I wanted it to be as bright as possible and even with that it still came out dark (and even while fading it looks blue have yet to see any green). I can't speak for anyone else but a genuine teal color is the unicorn of hair dye in my world- i've been dying and cutting my own hair pretty much only using semi/demi hair dye for over 10 years now and in all that time I have yet to find a genuine teal color. I've pretty much tried every brand I could get my hands on with zero luck- it's either dark blue with teal highlights/shine like this one, 98% green with 2% blue, green, dark green, blue, etc. I know going to a salon is an option and is probably my best bet to get genuine teal but because of my failings for the last decade i'm terrified of spending a couple hundred dollars just to end up with a non teal color again 😣. What in the world is going on? 🤣 It's not the olden days where getting colors is impossible and we had to make our own colors using rare to find items it's 2022 so surely there's a way to get a GENUINE TEAL hair dye!

3.) I can't speak for anyone else but in my experience this is hands down the thickest hair dye i've ever come across. This wouldn't of been an issue for me had the bottle design been the same as a lot of other semi/demi hair dyes are (a short easily accessible resealable cylinder) but since it wasn't and instead was put into a thick, dark and non flexible bottle it was next to impossible to get all the dye out or even see how much was in there. To get it out you either have to mix in some really watery hair conditioner or cut the bottle open and hope you don't hurt yourself or get dye all over the place in the process. While the design is visually really cute it's not practical- you end up wasting a lot of dye because you can't get it all out, in an attempt to get the remaining dye out you have to risk injuring yourself or getting dye all over the place or diluting it, since the bottle is black you have no idea how much dye is in there when you first get it so you won't know if you've been ripped off or not after getting a lot out you'll have no idea how much is still in there, because the dye is so thick and it's badly designed you end up having to constantly hit the bottom of the bottle/squeeze on it really hard/shake it hard etc just to get it out which after 20+ minutes really hurt my hands, you can't use the dye right out of the container like you can with the other cylinder hair dye containers and finally because you can't store any left over dye- the opening is so darn tiny there's no way you'll be able to get this thick dye back inside to use later on.

4.) This cost me $12.99 plus tax per bottle (it took 4 bottles to do my hair because I have really long thick hair) and when I bought it the price didn't bother me in fact it's pretty much average as far as semi/demi hair dye goes (the cheapest hair dye I use costs $10 a piece and the most expensive I use is $15 a piece so this is right in the middle) but after taking into account that it's not a genuine teal color, how insanely quickly it fades, how unpractical the design is, that I can't store unused dye, how much ends up going to waste and all the other negatives the price is definitely not worth it to me.

5.) If you've used semi/demi hair dye as much as I have then you already know about the notorious staining and bleeding that comes with these types of hair dyes haha but FYI this one is worse then what you're used to. With every other semi/demi hair dye i've used by the second wash the bleeding stops, the staining on my skin and ears has gone away, it doesn't stain my skin and ears while wet, scratching my scalp doesn't result in stained fingers and dye under my nails and my fingers won't get stained while I wash my hair but with this dye all those negatives have continued all the way past the 4th wash. Basically this dye has all the negatives of semi/demi hair dye but NONE of the positives 🤷🏻‍♀️

So all in all I really don't like this hair dye and wouldn't recommend it. Tbh the only thing it has going for it is that it does make my hair feel really soft and doesn't leave a weird coating on my hair like some other semi/demi hair dyes do but that doesn't mean much when everything else was a fail. Now that I think about it though I think this dye would be perfect for people who either only want crazy colored hair for a short period of time (like for a halloween costume, cosplay, an event, etc) or for parents whose kid's want to dye their hair a crazy color because it fades really quickly and isn't bright at all and is pretty mellow for semi/demi dye, as for vets like me who actually want long lasting bright color STAY AWAY 🙏🏼😂

title: Upgrade to the Mach 3 for a better shave, easier cleaning, and cheaper cost per week.
text:
I have used these razors for about 3 years. I'm a dry shaver, so a good, sharp razor is very important to me.

The one really big fault of these Customplus blades is that there is no place for the cut beard to go, so it packs in between the blades. (As I dry shave, I simply tap the razor on the sink every stroke or two to keep it reasonably clean.) The Mach 3 and Fusion have the open backs, which are almost self-cleaning, so I prefer that design.

Each razor lasts me a week. The first shave is great and the 2nd and 3rd aren't bad. 4th to 7th get worse and by the end of the week I WANT a new razor.

When I first became aware of these a couple years ago, they were priced at about 20% of the price of a Mach 3 blade. Now in 2014, they are about 1/2 the price of a Mach 3 disposable. What has happened is that the price of these razors has doubled, while the Mach 3 has stayed the same or even come down a bit.

Now the Mach 3 is a great blade, and I can get 3-4 weeks out of one, with a better shave and easier cleaning - all at the same cost per week, or even cheaper. In my opinion, the Mach 3 is at the best cost/performance point.

The Fusion? I used my initial blade for a whole year, though I have to admit that sheer pride kept me gritting through the pain through the last few months. The replacement blades only lasted a month or two before I couldn't stand them anymore. In my experience, they are still way overpriced compared to the minor increase in performance over the Mach 3.

Doc Martin's Nextgen is a good substitute for the late Bullfrog Surfer Formula: it's easy to apply, it works for hours and hours, it stays put, but it's easy to remove when you want to remove it. I expect to be a repeat customer.

title: Great shaver
text:
[[ASIN:B000UJZIEY Philips Norelco 8060X Moisturizing Shaving System]]
This shaver was bought for me after careful studying of the reviews on Amazon. Now after three weeks of shaving I can say that I am quite satisfied.

The tool is very quiet, gives a good close shave, almost as good as a razor shave. The shaving is a very pleasant experience, thanks to the wet foam or cream that is used on the face during the shave. I have tried both the special Nivea lotion and regular shaving foam. They work equally well. No hair or foam is spilled onto your shirt or over the sink.

A good shave takes roughly 5 minutes, more or less the same time as a good razor shave. The cleaning of the shaver is very easy, a quick rinse under the faucet.

All in all, the shaving experience is very similar to a razor shave. The advantage is that the shaver never cuts you, something a razor blade cannot achieve.

The only drawback is that the batteries should not be overcharged. Therefore you have to make an effort to stop the charging process after 90 minutes. (If you overcharge for a few extra hours nothing bad seems to happen with the shaver, but Philips writes that overcharging is not good for the lifetime of the battery.) It is a pity the battery charger does not have a simple timer for this charging problem.

I compared the shaving comfort of this wet shaver with the shaving comfort of my fiends Philips dry shaver [[ASIN:B001AMRQ2W Philips Norelco SpeedXL 8240XL Men's Shaving System]]. I must say the dry shaver was less pleasant and more irritating to the skin. There was no time saving when using the dry shaver.

text:
These come in a resealable ziplock bag. Inside the ziplock bag are 3 individual product boxes. Each product box holds 1 pencil and 1 sharpener. I initially thought that there wasn’t a sharpener included like the product page said, but then I saw it at the bottom of the box (I show a photo). You just need to make sure you really get it in all the hairs and use it to move them into place, then run a spoolie through to spread it around better and blend it out because you do get some areas that get more wax than others, so the spoolie helps spread it around. Overall, these are okay. For me, I needed to work applying the wax pencil to my brows a lot more than when I add clear brow gel. title: Not as Strong As I Hoped
text:
I am relatively new to solid colognes. I own this sampler set, Oak City Beard's Sandalwood Bourbon, and a sample set from another company. The other company's set was my first venture into solid colognes. I liked the variety it offered, and their colognes usually lasted most of the day.

I expected the same from this set.

I will admit, I liked variety that this offered, which is why I ordered it. Now that I've had time to try out each one, here are my thoughts. (Please note, cologne can smell different on each person, so what didn't work for me, may work for you.)

Barista - I don't drink coffee, so the thought of smelling like coffee all day was not a selling point for me. I figured this would be my least favorite of the four. When I opened the tin, it smelled like a 30-year-old motel lobby. A powerful scent of cheap black coffee, with a hint of musty cigarettes and pleather couches. I was not impressed. Still, I put it on and the smell changed to more of a 1990s coffee shop. Fortunately, the cocoa smell came forward more once it was on me, and the coffee was not as strong. I don't hate it as much as I thought I would. In fact, I kind of like how it smells on me.

Woodland Ranger - My favorite out of the bunch. While you may think it would make you smell like a Christmas tree, it's more of a clean outdoors scent.

Snow Leopard - I love me some sandalwood, so this was the one I really bought the set for. It says there is peppermint in it, but I can't smell it. Also, I feel like the vanilla overpowers the sandalwood. Not as good as I had hoped. Not bad at all, just not what I expected. (This one also seems to dissipate quicker than the others.)

Uncle Jack - I smell the bourbon and a trace of tobacco, but once again, the vanilla is the stronger scent here. It's definitely not a bad smell, probably my second favorite of the pack.

As I mentioned in the headline, the colognes are just not as strong as I hoped for. title: It’s Okay, But Not For Me...
text:
This is okay but there’s a few issues I have with it....

First, the mirror came with a little chunk in the corner gone. It’s not a big deal because it’s so small, but it would be nice if the mirror would have come better protected so that it wasn’t missing a piece no matter how small.

Second, this doesn’t really hold much unless you want it to be all separate parts. If you have it all put together with the side trays sitting on each side of the big oval tray, the silicone pieces over top the side trays, and the square tray sitting in the middle of the big oval tray - Then you can’t hold much with it. The side trays with the silicone pieces only hold so much. The one with the lines you can lay brushes in the grooves like shown in the photos on the product page. But, there’s only 4 grooves where brushes can actually lay, and more than 1 or sometimes 2 brushes is all that fits in each groove. The other silicone tray has the X’s that you can put things in so they stand straight up. There’s 11 small ones and 8 big ones. The big ones you could potentially fit more than 1 item in. Also, the middle tray part that the mirror goes over as a lid, if you’re going to do that, then you can only have items in that tray that the mirror will be able to lay flat over, so that limits how much and what you can place in it. If you have it all put together, then it doesn’t take up much room. But, if you have it all in separate parts (like the first photo on the product page), then it takes up a lot of room for not holding too much. I might as well keep using my cups or brush holders for my brushes, which hold a ton of brushes, and plastic or acrylic drawer organizers.

Third, I don’t like how the mirror just sits, it isn’t actually attached. It comes off so easy. One little bump and the mirror falls over. It would be nice if they would have that attached somehow so that it would fold down over the tray but still be connected.

Finally, it’s supposed to be easy to wash and dry. To me, the silicone pieces are not easy to clean. The dust collects on them like crazy. And I try to just wipe off the dust with a dry cloth but the silicone is rubbery and the dust just kind of sticks to it. If you use a wet cloth you’re able to get the dust, but you have to work really hard to get it off. I just don’t like it.

Overall, this just doesn’t work for me. I wanted it to organize things while taking up less space. But, when it is taking up less space, it doesn’t hold enough for me. If you’re looking just to hold a few small things. Like you have some small items that you just want to have a place, then this might work for you. As long as you don’t mind that the mirror isn’t attached and might come off easy.

title: They recommend to use it in the morning on DRY skin
text:
I bought this serum from ScienceSerum directly and returned it after 3 weeks of use since it dried out my around eye area beyond repair. Skin in the corners of my eyes started to crape, lines and wrinkles became more deep and pronounced because of the dryness, puffiness and dark circles appeared. It has been 4 weeks since I stopped using it, but I still have been able neither to quench the dryness nor diminish puffiness no matter what I do. I went to my derm, he said I have severe allergic reaction and prescribed steroids to combat the symptoms.

At the time when skin care layering is paramount, this product is a huge logistical failure.
It is very difficult to incorporate the serum into either- morning or night - routine. They recommend to use it in the morning on DRY skin, which means you would need to cleanse your face, wait for it to dry, apply it, then wait again for the serum to dry. Who has time for that much waiting in the morning? Another issue for me was that I could not leave my skin dry for that much time without applying toner and Vit C. But then, when the serum was dried, vitamin C would be washed off along with the serum. I wrote to the company and asked them how to properly layer it with other skincare products I use (Vitamin C, Retin-A, essences etc) they had no idea!
Another problem - it is extremely difficult to get it off your skin completely without pulling and tagging your delicate eye area. But if you do not pulling and tagging, the product stays on your skin and destroys it very rapidly.
If you have a question and write to Scienceserum, be prepared to contact them at least three times before they respond.
If you are going to buy directly from them and decide to return the serum, you will be responsible for return shipping AND they are going to withhold 20% of the serum cost for the original shipping. Returns are processed only on Mondays, so do not expect the return money to be on your account soon. The last drop was when I wrote to them about my experience, I received back one line reply consisting of the return address". No word of apology or concern.
Overall, it is a dangerous, damaging product, please be very cautious before buying it.

title: Effective for the job, may still be scary to young children though
text:
This arrived packaged as another reviewer depicted in a picture.
I was able to use the trimmer immediately after opening it. I watched a few YouTube videos on how to give a buzz cut and set off. My son was not in a mood for a haircut at the time after having just got back from out of state so it was a bit of a challenge. It was as if he was hula hooping with his upper body without the hoola hoop.

Halfway through the cut I felt the need to plug in the trimmer to see if it would have more power. I know the lower noise is supposed to make it not as unit imitating toward young children but it just didn't seem as powerful as a more professional trimmer. I couldn't exactly just buzz off my son's long hair in one swoop. I had to pull out some scissors and trim off the length before I could really start trimming toward the base of his head. It took awhile to get the look I desired. I used the 12 mm attachment since his hair is still very fine and I wanted some room for error in case I had to get any mistakes cleaned up by a hair stylist later. I did cut a line is his hair without the attachments on while attempting to trim behind his ear so that could illustrate that the base trimmer is effective in cleaning up hairlines. I did actually clean up his neck hairline but the way I used it kind of scratched the surface of his neck.

The design of the trimmer is simple. There's a basic indicator light that is green when turned on with a side button and it is red while charging.

Overall, I feel the trimmer is effective in doing its job. I believe for some little kids that a trimmer is scary regardless of how you design it. My son's first haircut was with scissors for that reason. It can be especially scary if you don't know what you're doing and have to take longer trying to figure it out with a new trimmer. I will give it another try when my son is in a better mood and my distraction methods work better.

As professional chemists, we analyzed this product (pH, FTIR, TGA, elemental analysis and GC-MS).  This alkaline product contains methylene chloride, methanol, n-butoxyethanol, a series of n-alkane hydrocarbons and two different petroleum boiling point distillate fractions.  Methylene chloride and methanol are known toxic chemicals which can be absorbed through the skin and inhaled into your respiratory tract.  Please use Google to search for and open the SDS docs for these two chemicals and read the hazards.  This product is similar to a methylene chloride containing industrial paint strippers which are being removed from the marketplace due to their toxic ingredient(s).  This product is not suitable for sale to the general public or to the professional nail community as a nail polish remover.  AMAZON is derelict in its duty to police the products it sells; in this case the product is highlighted as "Amazon's Choice". title: Electrolysis ain't easy but it works
text:
I'm giving this product a five star review because it actually does work. It might not be working consistently or easily for many users because electrolysis is actually pretty hard to do. That's why there are professionals who do it full time as a job. This product uses galvanic electrolysis. There are two other types that professional users and equipment can do. However if people are patient and follow through with good technique they will get good results eventually. And electrolysis is the ONLY permanent method of hair removal that you can do on your own. Anything else, however easy and painless, is just a temporary fix. So the product should not be judged by how difficult it is to use, but by the permanence of the results.
-Hair grows in three phases. Electrolysis only works best in the initial growing phase and sometimes works in the intermediate phase. It will not work in the final, dormant stage because the root, which electrolysis kills, is not active. An easy way to make sure you are only spending time on hairs in the growing phases is to shave an area and wait a few days. The hairs that poke up are growing.
-It only makes sense to do electrolysis on terminal hairs. Those are the dark, coarse hairs. Vellus hairs, the light and fine ones, are not that compatible with electrolysis because the holes they grow out of are small like the hairs themselves and aren't very easy to thread the needle in to all the way. There's also a risk of scarring. So don't go nuts. Just focus on the terminal hairs.
-Electrolysis kills hair roots through a combination of heat and a corrosive, lye-like substance that results from the electric charge coming in to contact with biological cells. That white, yucky substance that people are complaining about? that's the "lye". Don't wipe it off and don't pluck the hairs right away. You want to let them soak in it a while and die. I treat a hair and then go brush my teeth or water the plants before I pluck the hair. The "lye" needs a few minutes to do the job of killing the hair root.
-You need to actually make contact with all of the root area and the sides at the follicle base to kill it. A hair root is sort of an elongated sheath shape not a little pin dot. If any cells survive it regenerates from the surviving cells. It's a good idea to sort of plunge the needle in and out very, very gently or jiggle it a bit side to side while treating a hair. This increases the area the electricity comes in contact with and improves the odds of killing all the root. It's better than holding the needle perfectly still.
-If you've killed the root the hair will slide out without any tugging and will feel almost "greasy". If you need any force to pull it out it's not dead and you should leave the hair in and wait a few days and try again.
-As you might be able to tell from my comments this is a pretty tricky process and the odds are against you. You need to hit the root perfectly, kill the whole root area and get it in the early phases of growth. I think electrolysis only really works well for targeting a few "crazy" hairs growing in weird spots. It's not that great for clearing large areas. Doing it requires focus and precision. And also a bit of luck. I had a half dozen weird hairs and I've used this product to kill them and am rid of them forever. For that, I consider it priceless. But if you are aiming to use it to clear large areas it's likely it will be a source of frustration. Even for professionals, with professional grade equipment and years of experience, clearing a large area takes months and months of detail oriented work.

Considering this shaver's apparent fragility, if you ever drop it you'll need a new one. Norelco switches have always been erratic, so leave the switch turned on and unplug the shaver to turn it off.
For the moment it does a good enough job, even without a closeness control. Its best feature is a full-sized trimmer, which works well.

She accidentally came upon these cloths on Amazon and was happy beyond words. So happy, she went and bought 2 sets of 4 cloths.

But, the feel of the cloth (dry) was not as plush as the original. The weave just wasn't as tight, and when she ran her fingers over the cloth, the fibers didn't cause any "drag". BIG difference. The new cloth barely even sloughed off any dead skin. To say my wife was bummed is to put it mildly. She sadly returned both sets to Amazon.

title: Somewhat underimpressed
text:
I got this razor as a Christmas gift after telling my girlfriend about it and it frustrated me a bit when it just didn't work as well as I expected it to. I thought I was going to have the most amazing shave of my life, and most convenient and comfortable to boot (especially for the price of this shaver). Well I'm sorry to say I eventually got a decent shave by the 3rd try, but as for my expectations well it just didn't happen.

Some background, I used to use a really basic Norelco triple rotary head as my first razor when I got it in my early teenage years to get rid of my meager beard. That was about 20 years ago, and I long ago abandoned using an electric razor. So even though I don't normally use one, instead preferring to use a triple blade and shaving gel every 2-3 days, I knew what to expect. And after reading the literature, the description/outer packaging, and viewing ads on TV I thought this unit would be head and shoulders about anything I'd used before.

I hate dealing with shaving and the possibility of any nicks/cuts/razor burn and ingrown hairs so in addition to avoiding that I wanted this for convenience and to save time, but the first problem I had with this shaver was that it took almost as long to shave using it as it would with my old razor and shaving gel. I used this Philips/Norelco 3 times to make sure I'd given it ample opportunity to perform and there wasn't any fluke, then if I still didn't like it I'd return it and go back to what I was doing or get something else.

Shave #1 - Fresh out of the box. Had about a 2.5 - 3 day beard going (I have a medium growth of mostly straight hairs) Was impressed how it felt and balanced in my hand. Unique flex head didn't flex as much as I thought it needed to, but probably not much of a detriment. Not atypical for me, but a good amount of hair to get rid of for any shaver. Used it to shave with dry skin. Had to get used to the most effective way to use/hold it, but it did well near my cheekbones (the easiest part), OK on my moustache and goatee area, and so-so on my jawbone and neck. Hardest part was my neck but also near my jaw. Had to go over the same areas several several times using medium pressure - much more than expected. And since I knew it takes a few shaves for your skin to get used to it and there is much more likely to be some discomfort the first time I thought OK no big deal. But I could tell there was a lot more "chafe" on my face than I expected and the neck area had quite a bit of razor burn / redness even though I really wasn't pushing hard or using it at what I would call a bad angle. Did not really cut the sideways hairs as well as I expected, since they advertise it will obliterate those and I have quite a few on my neck. Rinsed the thing under water, dried with towel and put it away. Put a bunch of lotion on my face to help, still feeling some light discomfort / itch all over immediately after.

Shave #2 - 2 days later. Opted to go with some water on my face since that is how I'm used to shaving and normally expect to get slightly better results, and a bit less irritation. It worked pretty well, but the shave still took around 8 minutes or so, a bit too long and I still needed a mirror the whole time. My face wasn't quite as irritated as the first time, meaning slightly less chafe and razor burn on my neck, though a few ingrown hairs had made themselves known directly under my chin from shave #1 and I did whatever I could to get rid of those with a tweezer beforehand. Sideways hairs still wouldn't cut quite as well as I expected, though I didn't quite have to go over my neck and rear of my jawbone quite as many times as the first shave. After this shave I still managed to have a few stray hairs that either would not cut easily even after 5 or 10 direct passes or (for a few) if they were facing sideways, then not at all. I went back with the tiny but fairly effective trimmer and knocked these out, but didn't expect to have to do this and added another minute or two to the process. Not much razorburn this time, put a normal amount of lotion on my face and I was good to go. Pretty good shave. Emptied the heads into the sink and rinsed and dried with water.

Shave #3 - 2 days later. Easily the best shave of the three, which was what I was hoping for. Still went with the wet shave, meaning I made sure there was plenty of water on my face to start. Again upper cheek was the easiest and took almost no time, then moustache, goatee, jaw and sideburns, and then neck. Initial shave took roughly 7 minutes. Not as bad but not what I would call super fast. The rotary heads got almost all the hairs this time, except for 1 or 2 stubborn / sideways hairs on my neck near my adam's apple. Some hairs / areas took 5-10 passes with the shave head but went away with the appropriate pressure/motion. Almost no razor burn on my neck and a pretty low amount of chafe. Was impressed how it got the hairs right under my nostrils this time, due to my practice and the shape of the head. After the shave, I had to go back to get about 3 hairs that didn't make the cut (literally). This again added 1-2 minutes of shave time. I applied the usual amount of lotion and rinsed and dried the heads. The weird thing was this time, for some reason due to the water when I opened the heads to clean it, there were almost no hairs inside. Usually with a dry shave and 2-3 days of growth the heads get pretty full quickly. But in this case there was none, and not many showed up in the sink or countertop either. Weird, I guess the water had some strange effect where they either disintegrate into much smaller hairs and/or made them fly out somewhere I couldn't see. Either way I was done. Still, I didn't think this performance was quite up to my initial expectations, or the billing that Philips/Norelco gave it as their "most advanced shaver". But, it was "close" to a wet shave with a blade. Maybe a 8 / 10 this time. However I didn't like having to use a mirror the whole time still. And for the price, especially since it's described as waterproof shouldn't you be able to take it in the shower for the ultimate convenience? I dunno, I figure with a top-of-the-line shaver from this company, you should.

I didn't bother with the cleaning / charging compartment since I didn't know if I would keep the razor or return to the store, and didn't want to learn something I wouldn't need to know, nor use up any of the shaving fluid or dirty it up if I planned to return. Just more hassle. I really think it's a little pointless to do this full cleaning process every time, maybe every few shaves but that's just me. Water works OK and the blades are billed as self-sharpening which means less worry and as long as you pat dry after the clean it should be OK.

The carrying case is the alternative charging mechanism, and you can take it with you on the go. It also comes with a slide-on head cover if you're just going to put the unit away say in a drawer until the next use and don't need to charge it. One problem, the plastic head cover that slides on doesn't work with the travel / charging case. Why they made it so this won't fit, I don't understand. You're prone to lose or break it I think if you can't keep it inside, and why else would they give it to you if you can't take it with you in the travel charging case?

My take is this shaver probably works best if you have a light or medium beard and you shave every 1-to-2 days. Otherwise, stick to a blade and heavy shave gel if possible.

Strengths:
- Good overall shave and closeness, with patience
- Reasonably comfortable shave
- Flexible head, very unique design adds an extra dimension
- Strong trimmer for the size
- Very quick 1 hr. charging in either the cleaning unit or travel case
- Works with wet or dry skin (warning: not designed to work in shower or submerged)
- Good for people with light to medium beards that shave every day
- Self-sharpening heads
- Motor seems strong and good RPM
- Cleaning unit makes maintenance a bit easier and worry-free
- 2 year warranty
- 30 day money back guarantee / trial
- Made in Europe, not China

Weaknesses:
- Price / Value
- Too many passes to get all hairs = longer shaving time
- Had to use a mirror entire time to get accurate shave
- Trimmer is absolutely tiny and I'm not sure how sturdy over time
- Plastic head cover doesn't fit in travel charging case, or have a home when not in use
- Doesn't cut sideways hairs near as well as advertised
- Charging and cleaning processes require more attention than desired
- Not good for people with very heavy beards who only want to shave every 3 or 4 days
- "Clean shaver" icon is not smart - it always appears even after rinsing heads under water
- Can't use in shower
- Overall, just not quite as 'advanced' as advertised

Time for me to bring this back and try another high-end shaver from another european-based company which should remain nameless.

title: Looks cool, but quickly overwhelmed.
text:
The Goldbox offer (half price) suckered me into buying this model, despite recently having happily switched away from Norelco to the Braun 360 Complete. One of the advantages of the Braun was the much better handling of longer whiskers as the occasional 1-week-slump generates. Hoping that the hype of the new shaving heads resolved this issue, I eagerly tried out the Arcitec. It's still completely overwhelmed and no competition for the Braun at all. For the daily shave, the Arcitec 1059X is quite able to provide a reasonable shave.

The design may be the main reason to get this model as the shape and the cool display are likely to grace every bathroom. It's modernistic, yet understated. Yes, this is one of the best looking shavers on the market! The shaving head is fairly flexible and adapts to contours well, As with any dry shaver I tried so far, it won't match a wet blade, but it's not bad either. In fact, with restricting the whiskers to a one or two day length, the results are fairly comparable to the Braun 360 which so far yielded the best results for me. Then again, past that point, the Braun is a clear winner loosing only to a wet blade (again).

Handling of the Arcitec is reasonable and style concerns certainly overrode function, but still to a subtle degree that's acceptable albeit not perfect. Battery life is excellent and the charging stand has actual suction cups to make it easier to keep the base planted on the counter top. There is also a travel case included which doubles as a charging cradle. (The power supply plugs into the case and contacts allow the razor to be charged when plugged in.)

Overall mostly a cool design and quite functional for the daily chore. However, if you're less diligent with your shaving schedule it's hopelessly overwhelmed with the longer (and thicker) whiskers. The lift'n'cut feature is standard for Norelco and reasonably effective. However, it also irritates the skin a bit more.

title: A True Gentleman's Walking Stick
text:
Alpacca is also named German Silver or Nickle Silver. Consisting mostly of copper, nickle and zinc content. In my brief research I find that Alpacca does not contain any actual silver. Though some may be silver plated. But do not think of it as cheap imitation silver. It is more akin to a subset of brass.

This Alpacca cane is the pricier big brother to the plastic headed walking stick of the same design. The plastic brethren of this stick was love at first sight. The flared head and modest fluting simply screams elegance. Nowhere have I found a more elegant walking stick for the 'top hat' era.

As reported with flared head sticks, it is better suited for show. The slightly rounded top makes putting any kind of real pressure uncomfortable without leather gloves. However, it does provide modest balance if weight bearing is not your walking issue. The silvery smooth head does not make the cane top heavy.

The rubber tip is pretty standard and is useful for standing the 3/4" wide cane on flat surfaces. On the negative side, it takes away from the distinctiveness and gives an "old man" quality. I ordered my cane through a vendor who does silver ferrules (plated brass tips) and upgraded the business end of this cane to become a "Gentleman's Walking Stick". Silver ferrules raise the value and elevate the distinctive beauty.

This Alpacca cane lacks the distinctive charm of a chrome collar. My vendor states he routinely heats up such heads for removal, but the extra cost hardly seems worth the upgrade. It was mostly due to removal of the head. Unlike the screw top plastic cane, the Alpacca head is hollow and intended for permanent mounting, using pitch.

As it stands, this cane is suited for mild assisted walking. Use it more for classy strolls, theater, special occasions and dancing. Do not forget the white leather gloves!

Addendum:
On Saturday, 2/7/2015 I finally revealed this walking stick for a big birthday celebration. My black and white clothing style makes me look good, but there is a "whoa" factor when seen with this stick and a pair of white leather gloves. It helps that I had the tip refined with a ferrule and small rubber tip. I love it.

title: Thought this was amazing, but now only like it..read UPDATE at bottom of review
text:
I’d been using the Sol De Janeiro Bum Bum Body Scrub. I looooove that scrub. It smells AMAZING and the smell stays with you. You know how most body scrubs smell nice but as soon as you’re done using it, you can’t really smell it on you? Well, the Bum Bum Body Scrub isn’t like that! It’s cute, but it’s a pain to open in the shower, get your hand in there and get some scrub out, and it dissolves pretty quick as water hits it since it’s a sugar scrub. So, I wanted a sugar scrub that was more affordable, but still smelled great, that wasn’t such a pain to get out in the shower, and that possibly didn’t dissolve so quick when water hit it. THIS SCRUB CHECKS ALL THOSE BOXES!

It’s way more affordable than the Bum Bum scrub. It comes in a jar, so you have to screw the top off, similar to the Bum Bum scrub. But, a lot easier. It smells amazing, like vanilla. It isn’t as strong smelling as the Bum Bum scrub, but I still feel like I can smell it on me after my shower. The BEST part....this is a “Sugar Balm Body Scrub.” The balm makes it kind of like a thicker, kind of paste. It is easier to pick up with your hands, spread on your body, and it doesn’t dissolve anywhere close to as quick as most sugar scrubs.

Overall, I LOVE this scrub! I will definitely replace it when I run out, and definitely recommend it!

UPDATE - The first few times I used this, I don’t know how I didn’t notice. But, when I was using it again, I saw a loose hair from my head on my arm, I went to pick it up and as I did, my nails kind of scraped against my skin. I felt gunk go under my nails. I looked and saw all this gunk under the 2 nails that scraped against my skin! I was like, “WHAT THE HECK?!” So, then I took my nails and scraped against another area I’d used the scrub at and the same thing happened. I remembered people saying this left a film on their skin, which at the time I initially wrote my review I didn’t feel it did. But, now I DEFINITELY say it does. BUT, it can be washed off. After I scraped my skin and found out about the gunk, I took a regular body wash on a wash cloth and went over the areas I’d used the scrub. After that I scraped my nails over the areas again and, thankfully, no gunk. So, you can get the residue off. Now, whether or not you want to go through scrubbing your body with this scrub and then go over it again with soap or body wash, that’s up to you. For me, it’s not a big deal because I like how this is a balm that doesn’t rinse away as quickly as a regular sugar scrub does. I like that I can spread it onto my body and then scrub without worrying about it melting away as soon as it touches my skin. So, I’m okay dealing with having to go over the areas with a body wash after using it. But, I’m definitely going to keep searching to find the perfect body sugar scrub that is affordable and doesn’t melt away quickly like this one, but that doesn’t leave a film I have to wash off after using it. So, I’m dropping my rating down from a 5 to a 3. I thought about only dropping it to a 4 since I still like it and am willing to deal with having to go over and wash again where I used it. But, it is still kind of a pain to have to do, so I decided to drop it to a 3.

title: Wouldn’t Recommend for Dry Skin
text:
I bought this hoping it would be a morning moisturizer. It came well-packaged and with a safety seal, and I have no complaints about the tube itself (easy squeeze tube for no mess and hygienic). The texture of the product is interesting—it’s thick and bouncy, and once it starts warming up on your hand, it applies fairly easily. There is really no scent, and there is a decent amount of product in the tube. The issues I have with the product, however, is the absorption rate and its spreadability on my skin (for reference, I have dry, sensitive skin). This stuff absorbs VERY quickly once it’s spread on the skin, which in this case is not really a good thing. It sticks to your skin where you spread it and doesn’t budge, which makes me tug at my skin inadvertently in an effort to massage the product more thoroughly all over my face. The finishing texture/spreading feeling on the face is very reminiscent of glue. On my skin, it’s also not nearly moisturizing enough—it feels like it’s just sitting on top of my skin.

I wouldn’t recommend this for people with dry skin, it’s just not hydrating enough. The spreadability and odd glue-like feeling of the product is also just not for me. I like thick and emollient moisturizers (for instance, the Bobbi Brown Hydrating Face cream is one of my all-time favorites) and so I thought I’d like this one, but it doesn’t spread or absorb very well. It feels almost more like a gel than a cream.

I do still use this product, but only for my neck as an added skincare step at night. I no longer use it on my face.

text: I ordered this for my wife, and she is thrilled to have it so that she can be ready when shorts and swimsuit season arrives. Not having to shave every day will be an absolute blessing for her. This SmoothSkin Pure Fit Intelligent Ultrafast IPL Laser Hair removal device comes with the device itself, a power cord, an optional precision head for use on smaller areas, and a detailed instruction book. Since this device does not work if the skin is too dark or the hair is too light, it is important to check the online skin suitability chart before purchasing to make sure that this device will actually work for the user. My wife's skin and hair color fell within the effective range, so she was good to go when this arrived. Also, since this device can make the skin photosensitive during the course of treatment, winter is the best time to start the initial 12 week course of hair removal. For those who live in a place where there really isn't much of a winter, just be aware that skin needs to be protected from the sun during this treatment period. Since my wife is still in the early phases of this treatment and it's already mid-March, she'll be cutting it kind of close. Worse case scenario, though, she can at least get a month or so of treatments done and then resume and/or start her treatment over again when winter is back. This SmoothSkin device has two modes for treatments, Glide, which is just like it sounds and is a continuous firing as the device glides along the skin in a steady movement, or Stamp, which is a single controlled burst at a time, designed for areas where you want tighter control over when and where the light fires, such as on the upper lip. There are also three treatment intensities, Power, which is the highest setting and good for larger areas, Gentle, for sensitive areas (also recommended when first starting IPL and getting used to how it feels), and Speed, the fastest treatment mode, for quickly covering larger areas and for doing fast touch-ups. This sounds complicated, but after my wife began doing these treatments once a week, she found that it was actually fairly easy to do. Granted, she is just doing legs and underarms for now, which are fairly basic. My wife's initial opinion of this SmoothSkin Pure Fit IPL laser hair removal device is extremely positive. Instead, I STRONGLY recommend that you check out the Gillette M3Power razor if you want the best quality shave. It seems like a gimmick, but it works. title: Horrible in every way, only for super sensitive skin. Will not give you exfoliation or deep pore cleansing
text: Four years ago I bought a generic version of the Clarisonic called the Nutrasonic. My little Nutrasonic quickly became my favorite four speed facial powerhouse. I loved my Nutrasonic (and still do) but sadly the company has decided to discontinue the brushes so my favorite little machine is no more. Hence I started shopping for a replacement and as before when I bought my Nutrasonic I was dead set on not getting a Clarisonic because of the high price of the machine. I came across the Philips Pure Radiance on Costco’s website and decided to order it thinking I would be happy with it since not only Costco but Amazon has rave reviews for the machine. I got the Philips yesterday and let me tell you this facial brush sucks big time. If you are used the battery operated facial brushes they sell at Wal-Mart, then you may like this weak inadequate machine, but if you are used to a powerhouse cleaner and exfoliater you will absolutely hate this machine as I did. First off, the Philips has only two speeds which are pretty slow. The brushes are super soft (even the supposed stiff pore cleansing brush) and the annoying timer that turns off the machine every 20 seconds to apparently remind stupid people to move to a different spot.  This machine was so weak and truthfully, I hated everything about this cleansing system as it did not leave my skin feeling clean what so ever. If you have super sensitive skin then perhaps this machine will be okay for you but those desiring a pore cleansing will be greatly disappointed. Beyond how weak the machine is in hindsight I should have thought about my current dilemma before ordering the Philips and that being the long term availability of brushes. Since facial cleansing systems are not Philip’s main seller I can guarantee that this machine will be like my Nutrasonic in a few years and have no brushes available. Sadly there is nothing nice I can say about this machine and can only say that if you are used to the Wal-Mart type of facial cleaners and not a Clarisonic then you will probably like this, but otherwise if you are used to the deep cleaning of a quality facial system you will certainly hate this machine. Of course I am taking this one back and have broken down to buying a Clarisonic for two reasons, the power of the machine and the future availability of the brushes. I can’t wait to get my new 4 speed Clarisonic Pro that I ordered off of E-Bay that cost me the same price as this Phillips did but will actually clean my acne prone aging skin.

title: It's amazing, unless you have hard water
text:
This review will be somewhat bi-polar, but this soap truly performs that way for me.

A quick TL;DR for those who don't want too many details: It gives an amazing post shave and lathers quickly, but that lather dissipates when created with hard water.

Onto the nitty-gritty. I have a plethora of artisan shaving soaps from the likes of Stirling, Mike's, Barrister & Mann, Catie's Bubbles, WSP, Razorock, etc... I also use some classic mass produced software like TOBS, Arko, Proraso, and some others. While I do like certain products more than others, I can typically get a quality shave from any of the products mentioned, and any of the razors I keep in rotation. However, I purchased Mitchell's Wool Fat because I had a specific need: a utilitarian soap that can protect me while I'm shaving my head. I typically only shave my head every 7-14 days (yes, this is absolutely doable with the right razors) so the job tends to require quality lather. I get great results from most of my artisan soaps, but the job is more time-consuming when I have to load up my brush from a container or the like. Creams work okay in terms of convenience, but they are a notch less protective than the artisan soaps. Another side note: I've veered more into fragrances in the form of EDT/cologne/EDP recently, so unscented shaving products are a plus for me these days. MWF and Arko both smell like cheap hotel soaps to me, and I have no problem with that.

I wanted a mug soap that could just live in a big, flat soup mug and be on standby for those head shaves. My first attempt at doing this simply and cheaply was with Arko. I crammed some into a salsa bowl, and it worked great for whipping up a large volume of lather very quickly. However, Arko loses its slickness when the lather isn't of the thicker variety, and it tends to function better as a cushiony soap. Yes, I'm aware that I can cram an artisan soap into whatever container I want, but I prefer to save those products (and their fancy scents) for when I'm savoring a more luxurious shave. I also wanted to try something that is triple-milled, very hard, and will sit properly in a mug without requiring pressing or manipulation, much how people used Williams and Old Spice back in the day.

Enter MWF. I knew this soap's reputation, and I knew that I was working with hard water, but I wanted to give it a go anyways because it's a classic that I'd never tried. This soap produces lather quite readily, actually. I tried it with synthetic, boar, and badger brushes. I always used as much product as possible, and bloomed the soap by soaking it in the mug during my shower. However, I'd always get similar results without fail. A very good-looking lather will be produced, and it will always begin to dissipate within seconds. Thicker lather? Dissipates. Thinner and more voluminous lather? Dissipates. Every time.

Fortunately, I still found it usable, because WOW this lather was incredibly slick, even after its partial dissipation. You can easily go over spots several times, especially if you apply some water to that spot. This slickness did a sufficient job of protecting my dome against cuts, but unfortunately there tends to be a bit more irritation and aftershave burn (nothing too excessive) due to the fact that this lather has insufficient cushion while being used with very aggressive razors. I tried to mitigate this by only lathering up sections of my head, then repeating that over and over to prevent the dissipation. This helped a bit, but the inconvenience was enough where I've unfortunately chosen to oust MWF from the very role I purchased it to fill.

This may read like a 1-2 star review, but here comes the good part. MWF, despite it's dissipating lather, repeatedly left me with the absolute best post shave feel I ever experienced. It soundly defeats even my 2 favorite soaps in this category, which are Stirling and B&M. I know that my skin loves lanolin, and I'm guessing the MWF contains a high concentration of lanolin, which unfortunately may contribute to it disagreeing with my hard water. The post shave is a hell of a payoff though, to the point where I'm glad that I tried it.

Bottom line, this product is not for everyone. If you're new to traditional wet shaving, then avoid it in favor of something more simplistic and easy to lather (TOBS, Razorock, or perhaps even Arko). If you know you have hard water, then steer clear unless you're just out to appease your curiosity. Personally, I'm split between disappointment and amazement. The post shave and speed of lather has wowed me enough to hang onto this soap just in case I end up moving somewhere with better water. I can also still use it for a regular face shave, especially with milder razors. However, this soap did end up failing me as a workman-like product that can provide high-end protection. I've since replaced it with a relative newcomer to the soap market, and the only triple-milled artisan soap that I know of: [[ASIN:B01L0ENB3W Fine - American Blend]]. No, it doesn't meet my desire for something unscented, but it does have that incredibly agreeable classic scent of barbasol, and I can't argue with that.

title: Just not good at all
text:
I'd been using a Norelco 5863 XL for years before this. When it finally kicked the bucket following an unfortunate water-immersion incident, I figured I'd go for its direct successor. Bad move. Norelco's manufacturing standards appear to have dropped precipitously over the last decade.

1. It just doesn't shave as closely as its predecessor. 2. The trimmer is just godawful. It's now spring-loaded, which is as convenient to open as the old one with a manual level, but comes with a really severe drawback - you can only use the trimmer by pulling down across your face, not by pushing up. If you try to push, the trimmer will just close, since you can no longer hold it open by holding you thumb on the level. I don't know about anyone else, but pulling is completely useless for me, thus making the trimmer useless as well.

3. The water-cleanable feature is a half-truth. Yes, you can rinse it out after use, but it still recommends you take it apart and clean with a brush once a month - exactly as frequently as the old non-water-cleanable model.

4. It feels like light cheap plastic [...] in your hand.

5. Sure the pictures on Amazon look ugly... but they really don't do it justice. This could very well be Darth Vader's shaver. If you've got a techno-dystopian theme going in your consumer electronics, then go for it... otherwise, you may want to reconsider.

title: Big disappointment (two reviews written a month apart)
text:
I bought the Alkatraveler stick when my home water ionizer went on the fritz and had to send it to Chanson for repair. I was planning a short trip as well, so I thought this would be a great opportunity to try out the travel ionizer.

I like the size of the device. It's very small, light and easy to transport. You simply drop it in a filtered water bottle or glass and allow it to alkanize the water (15 min or so). Supposedly it raises the pH level by 2 points, but I have not tested this yet. The stick comes with a cheap piece of plastic tubing for storage. I opted to use a paper towel and zip lock bag. I shake out the ionizer and wrap it in the paper towel to absorb any excess water.

The main reason I gave this product only 3 starts is that it is difficult to retrieve from the water. You have to use an implement, like a spoon or tongs to get it out, or else you have to stick your fingers in the glass to get it. You want to submerge the stick so that requires at least 8 oz of water. While traveling, I used a wide mouth plastic bottle to ionize the water, and then poured it into another bottle to drink. It would have been much easier if the device had a chain like a tea infuser ball or something to help remove the stick from the water. I sent feedback to the company and received this reply: "We see your point, and will forward your recommendation. The way the Alka Traveler stick is designed now will not allow a chain to fit in the bottle cap carry case. Thank you for your suggestion."

So, although I was glad to have the device, it is not as convenient as it could be.

8/10/13 Update: I've been using this alkaline stick for almost a month now and I am pretty disappointed with it. I had to resort to keeping the stick immersed in water while I drank since there was no easy way to get it out of the container. Also, I started testing the water for alkalinity. The product description claims the stick raises the water alkalinity by 2 points. I tested my filtered water first, which resulted in 7.0 every time. During three separate tests I left the stick in for 10 min, then 15 min, then 20 min. Every time the water tested at barely 8.0. It never reached 9.0 as I expected. So this product barely raises the alkalinity level. Big waste of money on my part.

title: Norelco 1050cc vs. Braun Pulsonic 9595
text:
I bought the new Philips Norelco 1050cc Arcitec Shaving System, returned it for a refund after 30 days, and then purchased a the new Braun Pulsonic 9595 Shaving System. Since I've had experience with both now, I thought my experience might be of value to others. I've had 3 Norelco shavers over the past 20 years. The 9595 is my first Braun shaver.

Shaving Closeness - The Braun definitely gives a closer shave and in less time, although the Norelco is acceptable. One reviewer commented about getting nicks from the Braun but I have not had that problem at all, even around the chin.

Comfort - The Braun feels heavier (I didn't actually weigh them) but I found the Braun more comfortable to hold.

Noise - The Braun is noisier, especially during the cleaning cycle.

Status Indicators on the Shaver - The indicators are better on the Braun; however, I've since learned that's mostly because I had the 1050 model. I now see that the 1060 or the 1090 models would have been better and probably would equal the Braun.

Charging/Cleaning Stand - The Braun is more convenient to replace the cleaning fluid but about the same cost (about $1.00 per week). Both seem to clean equally well. The charge and cleaning status lights on the Braun are easier to see and give better status information. But the big difference here is the way the charging system works. With the Braun, you simply place your used razor in the stand, push a button, and the cleaning & charging are taken care of. However, with the Norelco, there are a number of warnings in the book to unplug the unit after it completes its cycle. This is a major inconvenience if you have to hang around and remember to unplug the unit. Also, the lack of an on/off switch seems a poor and cheap design.

Trimmer - To even off my sideburns, I found the Norelco somewhat difficult to use because the trimmer did not stick out far enough beyond the shaving head. This was not a problem with the Braun.

Cost - The Braun cost about $20 more.

Return Policy - 60 day money back with Norelco; only 30 days with Braun.

Bottom-Line - I started with a bias toward the Norelco because of my past experiences but in my opinion, this new Braun definitely surpasses the Norelco in terms of shaving closeness and convenience. Braun is clearly worth the extra $20, although the Norelco is a decent product.

I was curious about a perfume for baby because we've been taught not to use anything on the little ones except the gentlest of lotions and body wash. I decided to give this a try because I was curious about the scent and the execution of a product like this.

First thing I did was smell this, and while it is a pleasant smell, this particular scent isn't my favorite. It is too floral for me, almost artificial. I may have liked and felt more comfortable using a citrus and fruity type of scent on my little one. I also looked at the ingredients list and while they may be free of parabens, phthalates, synthetic colors, dyes, GMOs, and Gluten Free, there are some potentially irritating ingredients for the very sensitive of skins. Ingredients like Linalool, Citral, Citranellol, Limonene can be an allergen. It may have prebiotics which is good but one good ingredient does not negate a potentially irritating one. I'm all for someone coming up with a safe and good cologne for baby but I'm not entirely sold on this product just yet. I did read up on some additional information but I need more convincing for me to be on board with this perfume for infants. I do love the story of why the founder wanted to create these scents for little ones but I'm just not fully on board with some of the ingredients used.

I'm not sure I will be using this on my baby but I think a more appropriate age is pre-teen or teens. I may have been a little more open to a "cleaner" perfume for that age range as I'm sure there's a market for that. From what I read, the founder is going to be launching perfumes for that age group, so that might be more appropriate.

My baby actually smells nice from good hygiene so he doesn't need anything else but I understand the concept behind these scents. Fragrances do invoke certain memories, just like music. There are certain scents that I get a whiff of and it immediately transports me back to that day, the person, or the memories of that particular time period. All that said, I will be holding off using perfume on my baby and will be spritzing this stuff on myself. I think the concept is great but I would like to see even "better" and cleaner ingredients if I am to use it on my baby.

I didn't see the ingredients list posted on this Amazon page yet so here it is:
Ingredients:
Alcohol Denat., Aqua (Water), Parfum (Fragrance) Niacinamide, Glycerin, Lactitol, Xylitol, Linalool, Citral, Citranellol, Limonene, Hexyl Cinnamal, Gernaniol, Amyl Cinnamal, Limolene, Hydroxycitronellal.

title: The Best & Cheap Electric Shaver You Can Buy! However You Get What You Pay For Though!
text:
UPDATE: 08-01-21

Its been nearly another year that I've owned these shavers, which makes a total of 3-years of ownership. Has my opinion on these shavers changed? Well, one just has to take a look at my updated rating and you have your answer. About a month after my first replacement, (which you can read about in the 2020 update) I discovered that the battery wasn't holding a charge as good as my first shaver, it got so bad that the charger would die, unless I had it plugged in all the time. This did not give me confidence at all!

Also, the cutting head from the get go, felt like it wasn't as sharp as the first shavers cutting head. I mean, we all know the blade isn't made out of Japanese steel but this is ridiculous, a new shaver head should be sharp! Because I did not want to write this product off too soon, I continued using the shaver for almost a complete year, and now the shaver head feels as dull as the last shaver after 2-years of use. For an entire year, this shaver was providing me a nice shade of red rash on my neck, nothing like walking into a store looking like you just came back from getting tortured by someone.

I simply could not put up with it anymore, and I am sorry to have to admit this, but I went back to a name brand shaver. I did my research, and I discovered that Panasonic was still making quality shavers made in Japan. I decided to also switch from a rotary design shaver, to a foil design shaver, as they provide a closer shave. The Panasonic Arc4 ES 8243AA is a much nicer shaver hands down! If you want to take 30-minutes for a red rash shave, then stick with Aefee, if you want a 10-minute shave that leaves you looking good afterwords, get the Panasonic.

Review has been updated to 3 out of 5 stars as of August 1st 2021...

UPDATE: 09-05-20

My wonderful shaver has recently been pulling my hairs, and taking twice as long to shave, which is due to the shaving head being dull. I went searching for replacement heads for my shaver, saw that there used to be some that were sold on Amazon, but they are out of stock, with no confidence that they will be back in stock, anytime soon. I saw that this shaver was still being sold to this day, and for cheaper then before! I thought, for 17-dollars, that would be about the same cost for a replacement head, for a cheap shaver, might as well buy a new one, even if my old one still works. I then decided it was time to go and update my review to reflect the longevity I got out of my old shaver.

Only to discover that it wasn't 1-year that I've owned my shaver like I thought, but 2-years! My oh my how time flies. That means, that I have been shaving on the original cutting head for 2-years, thats unheard of for electric shavers, holy cow! So there is my longevity review guys, 2-years, still kicking, just needs a new head, but no replacement head in stock. 17-dollars is all I had to pay to buy a new shaver, its a no brainer. So, guys, if your looking for a shaver that is going to get the job done, this is what you need. Now, if the company can get replacement heads back in stock that would be great. But for now, you can just buy a new shaver when your head goes dull.

I am keeping my review at 5-STARS! :)

Original Review:

I have used several electric shavers in my life, all of them being Norelco. I was never a fan of the two-bladed shavers, I grow a thick beard, and it just takes too long to shave with those things. The 3-bladed shavers can be hit or miss depending on brand/model. Norelco used to make quality shavers back in the 80's and 90's. Since Phillips's acquisition of the Norelco brand however, the quality has gone down drastically. Many reviews complain of underpowered motors, motors burning out early, and poor shaving quality, unless of course you buy the high end 200 dollar model, then your in heaven lol.

Thankfully these day, we have a choice. I don't know about you, but I am not in the rich income bracket, I can't just dump 200 dollars into a shaver just to get something that is quality. Fortunately, there are many different types of shavers made in China now, that are much more affordable. What sold me on this shaver, is that it uses a 800MAH lithium rechargeable battery, that can be charged via USB. It uses a pretty blue LED battery indicator display, which shows minutes of run-time remaining.

It uses a standard 3-bladed system, with a pop up side-burn trimmer. It is also easy to pop the blades off and clean them, and even though I didn't require this feature, it is also IPX7 waterproof. The shaver comes with a nice velvet pouch, a brush, USB cable, and a operators manual. When I turned the unit on, I couldn't believe how quiet this thing runs, most certainly quieter then the old 80's - 90's Norelco models. So the question you might be asking is, how does it perform?

If all you have is stubble, you can expect this to provide a pretty smooth shave within a reasonable amount of time. I just did nice and slow rotational movements, as you are supposed to do with this type of shaver, and it did a pretty good job! If you let your beard get beyond a stubble, as one would expect, it does take longer to get the job done, but the shaver was able to do it, and seemed to have enough power, not just in time duration, but also in horse power.

Since I did not do a wet shave with this, I can't speak as to its effectiveness. I bought an electric shaver for the convenience of a dry shave, as wet shaving is a pain in the but for me. While the water proof rating allows one to simply run the head under the water stream to clean it out, I however just used the brush that they supplied, and some canned air, and it did just as good, without fully taking the blades out of the head. Recharge time is faster then they state when utilizing a powerful Anker wall charger that puts out 3 amps. I charged my battery from 45 minutes left, to 60-minutes left, in only 20 minutes.

In conclusion, I believe this to be a very nice electric shaver. And for the price I paid for it, I expected it to be weaker in construction, however, that is further from the truth. The construction of this shaver is top notch, and rivals higher end Phillips Norelco's in my humble opinion. If you need a quality electric shaver that will get the job done, and doesn't break the bank, I highly recommend this one! 5 out of 5 stars!

title: Not great at first but now I like it
text:
I really struggled with this nail stamper at first. It did not work out of the box for me like it did for other reviewers. This is essentially what worked for me.

1. I washed the stamper head with dish soap. After it dried, I did a very light swipe of rubbing alcohol. This will be the only time I ever treat it with anything but soap and water (in order to protect the ability to see through the stamper).
2. The stamper head is very squishy. This makes it a dream for transferring images onto your nails (it can get down in the nooks and crannies). But a squishy stamper head can make picking up the image from the stamper plate tricky. The best thing you can do is to work fast. Scrape the plate lightly with your scraper at a 45 degree angle with one hand and have the stamper ready with the other hand to immediately pick up the image, pressing straight down and not to hard.
3. Once the image is transferred, you have a little time to line it up but you will still need to work quickly. The image should be transferred to your nail within 5 seconds for the best chance at a succesful transfer.

4 stars from me since I was able to figure it out and get it to work pretty nicely. And the price is very low. However, getting to that point was quite frustrating. I would have appreciated some instructions and trouble shooting tips to come with the stamper. Hopefully my review will help anyone who buys this.

title: Good conditioner for the right hair type, contains silicone and LOTS of fragrance
text:
There are a number of MoroccanOil products I really like but for me and my hair, some products can be hit or miss. I generally try to avoid silicone in hair products (especially the ones that are not water soluble as they can lead to build up). Fortunately, the types of silicone in this product all appear to be water soluble (a good thing if you don't mind silicone on your hair). This ingredient is likely the most effective one in the list to give hair that satisfying "slip" while reducing frizz and making it easier to comb through.

There are also a lot of other great ingredients but notably, fragrance is pretty high up on the list which seems to be common with MO products. I didn't have any sort of reaction but others who may have sensitive skin could.

Overall, this is a decent conditioner but can be a little heavy on my fine, wavy hair if I put it too close to my roots but that is true of most hair masks I use as well.
