title: Great for making buns, and helps curl your hair too!
text:
I had one of these when I was a kid, and I LOVED it, but at some point I got rid of it, and I really wish I hadn't. This "Hairigami" or whatever you want to call it is AWESOME. I have long hair that doesn't hold a curl well, but after I put my hair up in this for several hours, my hair comes out almost perfectly curled in a really natural-looking way. It does take some practice to get it right every time, but once you know how to do it, it's super quick and easy. I took some pictures to show my friends the steps, so I figured I'd include them here too (sorry for the quality--taking pictures of the back of your head isn't easy!).

STEP 1: Place your hair between the two arms (I don't know if that's the technical term, but that's what we'll call it here). I took these pics after I'd already had my hair up in this thing for a couple hours, so that's why my hair is already curly (my hair is very straight and thick)

STEP 2: Drag the Hairigami down a little over halfway down your hair (I tried to roll it up from the bottom of my hair the first time, and since my hair is slightly layered that was impossible to do. Also my arms aren't long enough to do that comfortably). Then, roll up until the Hairigami is snug against your head. (Note -- roll UP, do not roll under, it doesn't work if you roll under, or at least it didn't for me)

STEP 3: Snap the Hairigami (which is basically just 2 cloth-covered snap bracelets) so that it curls into a bun. This is a great hairstyle for work, or anything really, so if you want to just leave your hair in this bun, you may need to gently spread your hair out so that the entire Hairigami is evenly covered. **NOTE: As a former dancer, I would exercise caution when using this for dancing. While it may feel very secure, the bun WILL NOT hold up well if you're doing lots of turns. It may work great for younger dancers who are not doing so many turns, but even then that's iffy. If using it for dance class, TEST IT FIRST to make sure your bun isn't going to unravel in the middle of class!**

STEP 4: After a few hours (that depends on your hair -- I only waited about 3 hours and my hair came out super nice and curly, but everyone's hair is going to be different), unroll the Hairigami and see how nice and curly your hair is!

Bottom line: this thing is great for making buns, and great to help curl your hair too. It seems like a weird invention, but it's actually great!

Steripod's Clip-On Razor Protector comes in a two-pack and was designed to fit 'most' razors. Inside the clip is a zinc strip Steripod claims keeps razors sharper longer.

Fabulous quality for an inexpensive, synthetic wig. I'm giving this wig 5 stars because it's so adorable, is of very nice quality and looks exactly as it does in the online picture. This is my first experience with a wig and I'm planning to just wear it on "bad hair days." Before using, I gently washed the wig with a few drops of mild, shampoo in warm water, and followed that, in the same way, with the conditioner product that came with that shampoo. I gently soaked it again in clean warm water, as the conditioner is a rinse-out type, then wrapped it in a terry towel to blot out most of the water, after which it air dried it on an open construction wig stand. With super gentle handling, it came out looking perfect.

I like my hair to be more sleek and smooth than puffy and wispy, so I even finished the little wig's salon treatment with a tiny bit of my favorite coconut pomade smoothed on with my fingers. Worked like a charm and looks great!
A major plus for this wig is that it has never shed at all through washing and subsequent styling. Several other inexpensive synthetic wigs warn that they will shed at first, and they do. Key concept here is: for optimal effect, be gentle, especially when brushing.

One challenge is that, like a couple of similar wigs I tried but did not keep, the inner woven cap is too big for my head. So, I took a few hand stitches in the nape area of the inner cap to shorten the distance of the cap from the front hair line to the nape area. That's where the problem is for me. It worked because the wig's hair is not really very thick and the cap is made of a wide-weave, soft mesh in the back, allowing me to create a one-inch, horizontal tuck across the whole back, between where the cap meets the ears. Don't know how long this will hold up, but inexpensive wigs like this one are not expected to last for ever, anyway.

And, I'll just repeat that this wig's hair is actually rather thin, so that if the color of your own hair does not readily blend in well with the color of the wig (for example, light blonde wig over dark brown natural hair) you could find some dark hair showing through, especially in the back. First off and to the bottom line, for quality and price point totally WORTH THE BUY!!

For reference, I ordered the 22 inch Color #2 Darkest Brown. I am 5'11" and ordered a length similar to my own hair.

Now for the background: I am mid 40s and I have always had SUPER thick, curly hair until an autoimmune thing kicked in at which point I lost 3/4s of that volume over a year. So I've been playing around with hair extensions. If we can dye out grays, do our nails, etc. to feel better about ourselves, why not hair extensions?? This particular piece is AMAZING! Honestly, it could be thicker, but then I feel it would be too heavy. It's perfect for me.

The color matches perfectly. The length is accurate. The sheen is beautiful. Some other reviewers complained about it tangling, and although it does, it doesn't tangle more than my own hair and brushes out back to original form with ease. ...Some other reviewers said it doesn't stay in place and I personally disagree. I straighten my hair, put it up in a ponytail at the height I want, clip in the extension, wrap the extra piece and secure with 3-4 bobby pins around the base. That may sound like a lot of work, but really it isn't (especially since I only wash my hair every third day or so, and in between days, I just shower without wetting my hair). It took me a couple tries to perfect it, but since, I have it down and wear it for 12-14 hours continuously without an issue. No headache, no slipping. My hair blends with the extension and you can't tell which strands are "real". ...Admittedly, I haven't played around with curling it or anything so I can't commit or advise on that.

All in all, I feel this is a cheap, quick and easy way to feel beautiful. And everyone deserves to feel beautiful! Hope this review helped :)

If you prefer untwisted styles, I suggest putting in the product all over your clean, damp hair, wait a day for it to dry, then add in the gel of your choice while gently detangling.

Either way I notice that while using it I retain more length, experience less breakage, and more scalp health.

Moral of the story: because of the formula changing over the past few years, this product takes a lot work if your texture is more kinky/coily. title: Not the best, not the worst, but a savior in times of Covid.
text:
I was disappointed when they arrived because the color was significantly darker than what is shown on the product page. Rather than golden blond and bleached blonde it was more like a mostly dark blond/light brown (with a reddish cast) with a little bit of bleached blond thrown in.

But I decided to work with it. I colored it lighter which ended up bringing out the red (not a good thing with my coloring), so I used a toner, and finally got to a point where they would blend in with my existing (and VERY spendy) extensions.

Although I don't look forward to spending $300 each time I have my existing extensions re-tightened and refreshed, it's a necessary evil and I'm not willing to go back to my thinning hair (radiation therapy, no thyroid, menopause and weight loss made me worry I'd wake up one morning looking like Jean Luc Picard.) But as the Covid months wore on, I found that an unanticipated benefit was that doing your own salon treatments at home saves a hella lot of money.

Fortunately, my husband was watching the first time I had my extensions installed. As I faced not being able to get them refreshed during lockdown, he suggested that I let him try removing the hangers-on and reinstalling the new ones. I was doubtful but fresh out of alternatives.

After watching every extensions installation video on youtube, he gave it a try. With some of my original extensions biting the dust during removal or the falling-out process, I needed a few extra to bolster the thickness, thus my purchase of these extensions.

PROS:
- Cheap. A fraction of the cost that I spent at my high end salon (which was over $1000 with initial installation). So, you can hardly argue with the cost.
- Once I got the color right, they seem to behave and feel the same as my existing pricey extensions.
- Shipped quickly.

CONS:
- Thinnish near the ends. Thickness peters out more than it should.
- Color significantly different from the thumbnail on the product page. (Probably less of a problem if you're not trying to match them to existing extensions and are not super picky about color.)
- Cheap enough to buy several and get a very thick mane o' hair.

WOULD I RECOMMEND?
Yes. With the caveat about color.

LONG STORY SHORT: I doubt I'll ever return to the pricey salon for extensions (unless these extensions don't stand the test of time.) Being able to buy these extensions and installation tools on Amazon, and being able to watch How To vids on youtube (and having a husband willing to do the deed) will probably save me about $2000 a year or more.

title: Works, but ergonomics seem off

First the good things. It works. In fact, I found the battery life to be outstanding. I took the toothbrush on a 12 day trip and it lasted that long despite only being rated for 10 days. It cleans your teeth pretty well. I also like the pressure indicator that lets you know if you're pushing too hard. Because it's fully functional, I don't feel like I can give it less than 3 stars. But here's why it doesn't get more.

First, the brush cycle. I've used other electric toothbrushes that also have the concept of a brush cycle, a beep, series of beeps, difference in the brush, whatever, that informs you to switch to a different area of your mouth. This toothbrush has that too and it works. Then it keeps working. The others I've used ran through the full cycle then turned off. This one, just kept going. You have to manually switch it off before it will stop. It's not a big deal since I know what part of my teeth I'm brushing, but it's part of the general behavior that I don't like.

title: Affordable Multi-function Device
text:
I was really impressed with the quality of this Ihelol Skin Rejuvenation Beauty Device, especially at such an affordable price point. (I've paid so much more for other devices that weren't as well designed or as multifunctional as this one is!)

It comes so nicely packaged! A bit of wrapping paper & a bow, or a gift bag is all you'll need to make this gift ready. At first I wanted the white version, but now I'm glad I got the Pink version instead, because it does give off sakura or cherry blosson vibes! I especially like the soft ombre effect of the coloring. The device doesn't come partially pre-charged, so you will have to charge it up for a couple hours using the included USB-C cord before first use.

It's great that there are 3 settings to match any of your skincare needs. And even though I know this is meant for use mainly on the face & neck, I think it can be great to use all over one's body as the contoured head conforms to all my lumps & bumps. (I used the heated red light setting on my left wrist/forearm to massage & ease my tendinitis achiness, especially during particularly chilly days.)

NOTE: If anyone has had any issues with getting their device to vibrate, it's super important to ensure these 3 things:

1) Remove the protective cover on the device head.

2) You must be making skin contact with the sensors on the handle & contact with another part of your body or face (not trying to use this device on another person), because these electrical impedance devices pass a low voltage current thru the body & require an entry & exit point. (Think of it like those scales that measure body mass by having you step on sensors on the scale while holding a bar that has other sensors on the handlebar.)

And last, but not least...
3) If you're dehydrated and/or have dry skin, it does make a difference of how effective this device can--or can't--be. Dry skin has a much higher electrical impedance than well hydrated, moisturized skin. Just as TENS or EMS devices require people to use conductive gels for electrode placement, it's really helpful to use these types of devices with your favorite serums or gel moisturizers. (Like if you've ever tried to use a fingerprint scanner & it keeps having trouble reading you, that's why people suggest putting on moisturizer before trying another reading.)

Also, with any skincare devices, or creams, or whatever it may be, please give it a minimum of a month of use before you judge if it did anything for you. Improvements take time & consistent use is key.

text:
I applied this to my 5 year olds blonde hair. I did not want to spend a future at a salon because.... she is five!
She DOES love the end result but I will say, if you want a successful process I have several important notes.
1. I can NOT speak to the bleach because we did NOT use it. I hear BAD things about it.... so, read other reviews if applicable.
2. Product is messy! That said; count on the NEED for 2 person application. Do NOT attempt to self apply this product. Will absolutely regret it and ruin your home and clothes.
3. Count on purchasing extra items AND plan for 3 hours from prep start to finish. I will explain why.
EXTRA ITEMS: This product will ABSOLUTELY stain hand, face and scalp. Purchase: extra gloves, vaseline, and hair dye removal!
GLOVES: It only comes with one crappy pair of gloves. For best result, swing by Sally's beauty and buy SEVERAL good pairs of gloves. OR buy some of those thick bathroom cleaning gloves that come to your elbows. this way you can use them and take them off and on easily to both apply AND rinse hair.
VASELINE: COMPLETELY coat ears, forehead, neck, etc with a THICK coat of vaseline to avoid staining
DYE REMOVAL: Swing by sally's and buy a bottle of hair dye remover BEFORE you start. This will get on skin and you will NOT get it off otherwise.
EXTRA TIME TO APPLY: I have applied this product in 4 different colors to both my own hair and others hair. I have NEVER gotten good coverage without having to apply it TWICE. (including this application. pictures attached are product of applying BOTH colors twice for an hour each time) For the vibrant color you will want, count on applying, waiting an hour to rinse. Blow dry and reapply for ANOTHER hour. Do not think you will "quickly" apply this product like a box of normal 20 minute color. You will be disappointed.

However, I have experience with this product so it was successful based on ALL the above notes.
Also, I DID experience severe staining to her scalp and it will NOT come off so far even with the hair dye remover. I did not apply it close to scalp but she is young and her hair is so thin, it bleed right through and left big nasty looking spots all over her little head. title: Synthetic Hair Blend
text:
I would never recommend this product nor will I purchase it again.

I ordered the 18" and 16" in 1B, 2 of each. I always wash and condition the hair before putting it in my hair and this hair washed beautifully! (pictured)

Upon straightening the hair before putting it in, I noticed the hair started melting on the flat iron......it was only set to 360 degrees though, which is LOW - yet it was still melting! (pictured) After about 3 passes, the synthetic parts melted/broke off and I didn't have any issues after. I noticed it was worse in the 18" but both lengths had issues with melting.

As far as shedding goes, it's the best hair I've ever had. My natural hair sheds more than this does. Maybe it's simply due to the fact that tape in are different than tracks or i-tips? Either way, it's been AMAZING (though I imagine other tape-ins are the same).

Longevity: I've had these in for about 4 weeks now and plan on taking them out at 6 weeks. I haven't experienced any tangling but the hair seems to "clump" slightly throughout the day. But when it's brushed out, it looks great. The ends sometimes look damaged.

Shininess: way too shiny for my liking. I wouldn't go as far as saying this looks like wig hair, but it probably falls in the middle of shiny wig and natural hair luster. Unless your hair is naturally really shiny, you probably won't like it.

Adhesive: I removed the original adhesive and put on Walker tape, so I can't comment on these falling out of my hair during wash day like the other comments. I can say that I wash and deep condition every week and let the conditioner sit in my hair for 1-2 hours and haven't had any issues with these falling out with Walker tape.

Packs Used: Though I feel like it would have looked fuller with all 4 in my head, 3 provided a natural look without fear of the tracks showing. I still have a few pieces left from the 3rd pack and plan on returning the 4th.

Overall, this is my first experience with tape-ins. Don't buy these - get something else.

title: Now I'm too sexy
text:
Now that I bought and used the T980, my cool slacker goatee is attracting too many women. I'm not getting any rest.

Naturally, a product that causes grief should be down-rated, but I won't here because this shaver is just doing its job.

And, we all like things with "turbo" in the description, however loosely that term is applied. It makes it go faster with a cool noise, so even in a shaver that is attractive to many.

Electric shavers for beards sure beat the heck out of scissors! The Norelco has a wide range of cutting depths and my beard comes out a uniform length. I did not feel any pulling or other discomfort. The charge seems to last for days and the charger itself, like the shaver, is a decent and modern design.

The little detail cutter is easy to attach and does a great job of defining the beard area and also clipping any stray hairs under the nose where the big cutter head cannot reach.

Some people think the closest cutting position is still not close enough for that short-stubble look and that does seem to be the case. I don't want mine that close, but I understand those who do and I take off a star for brotherly solidarity. Actually, I'm sure that if it was to cut more closely, that would take it into the realm of regular shavers, an expensive world of high-tech blades and lubricants. Actually, if you press down a little, you can get closer.

The turbo thing works well. It vacuums almost every hair into the storage chamber. I didn't expect the vacuum action to work so well. I think the turbo button should be the only button, but there it is. The non-turbo setting is less noisy...

The parts detach easily and the little supplied brush works well to clean it out. The little travel pouch is nice.

The T980 works just as it should, for me, and the price is reasonable. I think it will last a long time and I am glad I bought it.

As for the women, I did exaggerate. One did make a favorable comment which is one more than before. That is an improvement, eh?

title: Ridiculously overpriced, but the performance is decent.
text:
I am conflicted about this product, same as I am with the sister shampoo. I think it's a great product in terms of quality and performance; I really like that it's sulfate free and not filled with a bunch of additives. I have noticed that my hair is very soft as a result of using this mask, so I will give credit where credit is due in that regard. It smells good, and it hydrates well, which is what it promises to do. I have no qualms with the performance, packaging, concept, or marketing of the product.

I am docking two stars, however, for the price point. I am all for luxury products and I am happy to drop money on products that work. However I think that the price is grossly inflated for the performance of the product. While it's a nice product, it's nowhere NEAR to being a $32 hair mask. With prices like that you're definitely in the middle of high end, luxury pricing for haircare products. To give you a few examples you could be purchasing Bumble & Bumble, Oribe, R+Co, and Kerastase for a similar price. I think for a mask that is going to be used regularly you need to offer a reasonable price for the product, especially given the fact that there are stronger, higher performing luxury products on the market. title: Works okay if you can draw line fast and get lashes on it, and line has to be thick
text:
A while back I tried an adhesive eyeliner for the first time. I had never heard of it before, so I honestly thought it was going to just be a gimmicky product and not actually work. I figured if something like that actually worked, why hadn’t I heard of it already?! I mean, lash glue can be a pain to work with. To have an eyeliner and lash glue in one, that’s amazing! That seemed like something people would be raving about, but I hadn’t even heard such a thing existed. But, I figured I’d try it out. I’m glad I did! That one actually worked well. It did end up drying out fast, but it worked. So, since then, I have been trying out different ones.

This has a felt tip. The eyeliner is pigmented, very black. The adhesive is sticky, but not extremely sticky. You have to work pretty darn fast with this. I have really small, really hooded eyes. So, when I wear liner, I like to tight line my lash line. I don’t want to be taking up the tiny lid space that’s actually seen with black liner. In order to tightline with a really thin line like I like, I usually move pretty slowly. Unfortunately, I can’t do that with this liner. I have to move fast if I don’t want it to dry and lose its stickiness. But, even if I move fast, the thin line like I like doesn’t cut it. The liner doesn’t seem all that sticky. But, it can be....

I always want to test adhesive liners before applying them to my eye. I don’t know if I’ll have some sort of reaction, so I figure it’s better to be safe than sorry. So, I draw a little line of it in my forearm. While I’m doing that, I give the liner a little test to see how it works. I drew the little line on my forearm. Then, I took a lash and stuck it to that line. The lash stuck really well to the line. It stayed on it well, even when I gave it little tugs. After that, I was really excited to try it on my eyes! I didn’t have any sort of reaction to the liner, so it was time to try it on my eyes....

I drew a thin line on my eyes, grabbed the lash and went to apply it. It stuck great to the last part of the line I had just finished drawing, but wouldn’t stick to the area where I started drawing the line. I didn’t know why, so I wiped it off and tried again. title: Meh. It's okay.
text:
Pros:
Makes hair less greasy.
Natural ingredients.

Cons:
Price is high for amount of product.
Application difficult.
Odd packaging.
Leaves ends of hair feeling coarse.

Personally, indifferent on smell.

I purchased this product because I recently switched to the "no poo" movement. I have been water-washing my hair two to three times a week for the last month and a half and loving the results. I needed a dry shampoo for some of those in-between days where my hair looked a little greasy and wanted a natural product without harsh chemicals. I found this and decided to give it a try.

I purchased the small size and it came in a salt shaker. The packaging is functional for the type of product, just a bit odd. It is slightly difficult to get the powder evenly distributed on my hair, though. I usually just get random thick spots of it and have to rub it in with my fingers (I find this works better than using a brush). I have to use quite a bit to completely cover my hair, as well. (I'm a guy with short-to-medium length hair; comes a little past the top of my ears when not brushed back.) Not sure how well this product would work for long hair - might be more difficult to apply. I also always end up with some of the powder on my face - never fails.

The smell is also a bit odd, but not unfavorable to me. I know some reviewers have said it smells awful, but it's a personal opinion. I don't think it smells bad or good - just interesting.

It does make my hair less greasy, which is the whole reason I purchased it to begin with. At first, it give a nice volume to my hair, as well. After an hour or two, though, it kind of flattens back out - which is not really a big deal to me, but if you're looking for this benefit, don't expect it. The ends of my hair seem to be a lot more coarse after use. Having shorter hair, it is difficult to just get it on my roots without touching the ends.

Overall, the product does it's intended purpose. Not really a fan of the application. The price seems very high for such a small amount, as well. Not sure if I will order again or look for a different product.

title: I wouldn't start with this--
text:
This is a beginner set, but it's not looking to help you-- No instructions.

Lucky for me--This isn't my first gel kit.

At first when I opened the box I liked how much they had to offer creatively. Some kits try to force a look, but this one was open to play with. Maybe not the best idea for a beginner kit- but I enjoyed that.

First the good:
I like this type of lamp when I'm doing gel- it's easy together both my hands in to hold the nail down when I first start, then I usually pick up the light and rotate it to get a full cure. Yes I have to restart the lamp a few times, but this isn't an expensive lamp so I don't mind.

I liked the little box they came in- sure it's cheep, but it was a nice tough to have (almost) everything in once place.

Then the annoying:

There are a lot of odd little problems, like the Gel itself, two are jelly clear and one is opaque. Opaque gel takes a little longer to cure because the light works a bit harder to travel though the nail. It would have been helpful if they mentioned that, OR only gave you one type of gel-so it doesn't confuse you-- but they didn't.

The nail forms were a bad fir for my hand. Thats just an unlucky break- all hands are diffrent- so im not including that in my rating, just something to mention in case they don't work for you too.

The colors were a little annoying to use, no color indicator on the bottle. this is common with cheeper sets, but I thought I'd mention it anyway- It can make doing your nails just a little bothersome.

The ugly-
they don't include slip solution-I ended up using my own from my nail kit, so I didn't have any problems, but that's a huge mistake on their part-- if you're just starting out you'll think gel nails are a sticky mess. Slip solution makes them manageable.

title: Not exactly for my tastes

I've been using various models of Philips Norelco shavers for the past 8 years and have always been happy with them. Each time I buy a bit more expensive model hoping I'll save even more time each morning...though I've never really saved much time!

Since this model was distinctly different from the others I had purchased before, I thought it would be a revolutionary new experience shaving in the shower and/or with moisturizing lotion. To be honest, the experience wasn't really any different and took me the same amount of time. The lotion adds an additional consumable requirement, and shaving in the shower seems such a waste of water. Not to say, however, that they don't contribute slightly to a great shave.

For those moments when I decide to shave OUT of the shower, the fact that there is no place for the stubble (cut hairs) to go besides down on you is a bit inconvenient. I understand why a model like this has such a requirement, but it's inconvenient when you're all dressed and you've got to watch for anything that might be on your shirt. I'm not shaving a beard everyday or anything but the good news is that most of the stubble seems to stick near the plastic head. As long as you rinse well after every use, you're probably in great shape.

It's a bit inconvenient, for travel usage, that you've got to carry around the charging dock/cradle and can't plug the AC right into the shaver. On the other hand, the shaver has a lithium ion battery (not familiar with many models with this feature) that seems to last a long time and charge quickly when needed.

Nonetheless, I'll still happily use this shaver. It does its job well, it's just that I'm not the target market for all the fancy wet/lotion features inside. Given that I rarely/never use the old fashioned razor and shaving cream, it's probably not a surprise. I'm guessing I'm not the market Norelco targets this model towards.

text:
I've been on a quest for a new electric razor since Christmas. I went astray and tried a Panasonic Foil type, and I won't make that mistake again. So now I knew it was Norelco or nothing. So which one? The top of the line 1090 was just too expensive for me to justify but then the price dropped and I got Amazon Prime all on the same day! Now it was doable and I'd get it the next day? Too much to take... I had to finally get it.

The new cleaning method alone is worth the price if you are a Norelco fan. It's so quick, and no removable combs and cutters to mix-up in the sink. Just flip 'em open and shoot a little hot water in there or run the whole head in hot soapy water. Done. Waaaay better system than any other Norelco shaver. It charges in only an hour and stays charged for a lot of shaves. 65 minutes worth. That's a lot of shaves.

Unfortunately the quality of the shave is not on par with other high-end Norelco shavers I've had in the past. It takes longer and you have to go over your face several times to get the same results and I used to get with my Norelco Spectra.

Lastly, let's talk about something that really doesn't matter. The looks. This thing is gorgeous. The pictures on this website don't do it justice. For one thing the materials it's made from are all top of the line. Carbon Fiber panels, and super rich "Black Chrome" accents on the front. Of course this thing is so good looking you might just be tempted to leave it out as an "art object" for all to see. It's a great looking razor that does an "okay" job of shaving. I don't know how people can say this thing shaves better than the old ones. It absolutely does not. It sure looks damn good though... Maybe Norelco can improve the heads on a future model and I'll give it another shot in a year or so.... For now? Stick with your old Norelcos. They do a better and faster job.

title: Planned Obsolescence
text:
Here are two things Phillips will not tell you about their Sonicare toothbrushes and heads.

1) The collar that holds the toothbrush to the handle will disintegrate in a couple of months. That's what prompted this review, because they would not replace mine after it fell apart two weeks after purchasing a replacement.

2) UNPLUG your base until you need to charge the toothbrush. If you charge it up overnight, then unplug the base, the toothbrush will work for four brushings per day for about a month. Then, when it signals or stops, plug the base in to charge it.

This method will allow your toothbrush to work for five years or longer. If you keep the base plugged in all the time, these NiCad batteries develop memory and will stop functioning after 18 to 24 months.

It's a nice, sharp cut.

The one thing I don't like is that as I make clips on my fingers, it ends up fraying my nails in different places. I end up with little white spots where each cut wasn't perfect. No other clippers I've used cause this. It goes away after 3 or 4 days as it gets naturally worn away, but it's annoying.

I suspect that it's because although it's a sharp cut, the surfaces of the blades (on BOTH of my clippers) don't mate perfectly and rip the nail away wherever those small gaps are. Closing them and holding up to the light, I see gaps. The toe clipper's gaps aren't as bad so the white spots are infrequent and I get cleaner cuts all the way across. The gaps on the finger clippers are more prominent, and I always get the white spots on all of my fingers. I'm not the type of guy who gets manicures, so I just want to do clean, even clips and be done, and not spend time filing if I already did a good, even cut...but I know women are particular about nails, so it bothers me that they may notice these white spots if I don't take the time to get rid of all of them.

title: Self-tanning product masquerading as an exfoliant
text:
For several years, I have used Mountain Majestic Arabica scrub (available here on Amazon). I obviously was quite pleased with it. I first tried it on my face, rinsed it off, and noticed when I towel dried my face there was brown on my otherwise white towel. Today, I used it all over my body as an exfoliant and ended up with a brown washcloth and another brown-stained towel. A couple more washings with soap seemed to get the brown off my skin, but not my washcloth. It will need to be trashed since it is now a reddish-brown mess. The stains on the towels are not as bad, and I can live with them, but I certainly would never put them out for guests. I have no idea how this product received an average of four stars.

If you want to ruin your towels and shower and dye your skin and hairline a reddish-brown, go for it. Otherwise, avoid this product like the plague. To replace my washcloth, scrub my shower (the guy at the big box store told me the $20 bottle of cleaner he sold me will remove anything), use twice the amount of Tide and bleach called for in trying to wash the dye out, it would have been much cheaper to use my old reliable brand.

As an aside, I'm not sure what type of oils they use in this product, but they are heavy and don't leave a nice feeling on your skin when rinsed off. Also, when reading reviews, start off with the bad ones. You'll get a better idea of the quality of the product in question.

title: Read & Heed the Negative Reviews
text:
I followed the product instructions, including testing on a small area before general application. The test removed some hair & had no negative side effects so I proceeded with the general application. I left the product on for 10 minutes with no adverse reaction. They came shortly afterwards when I got into the shower & began to wipe the cream away using the glove that was provided. I immediately experienced a burning sensation that increased in intensity as I proceeded. I gave up using the glove & rinsed away the remaining Bare Balm with lukewarm water & my hand. By now the skin was so sore that I could barely stand to let the water touch it but I realized that I had to remove all of the Bare Balm so I persevered. I then blotted the area dry with a towel and applied the Calm Balm with my bare hand. Even those light touches hurt like hell.

That was yesterday. I have been "going commando" since then, wearing only sweat pants. I was awakened several times during the night with pain as the affected area touched sheets or even my leg. Any contact whatsoever, whether with fabric or other skin, is still painful today. I packaged everything up for return and applied a different skin cream today to aid in healing. As before, even the gentle touch of my fingers hurts.

Oh yeah, before I forget, the Bare Balm did not even remove all of the hair. Still, I have heard that the base oil is good for skin as well, so that is a plus as well.

The main minus I have here is that while the smell here isn't awful, it's still strong enough that it gave me a bit of a headache. (That's another reason I probably won't be using it on my face.) I was able to deal with this by putting it on in small bits, which seemed to work well since the strongest part of the smell faded away pretty quickly. I do have to commend the company for their packaging. While the bottle did leak during transport, the company was aware that this would happen ahead of time and packaged this well. text:
This thing looks very nice, and feels even nicer! It’s beautiful, and very easy to use. However, it is difficult to grip at times, especially if your hands are wet or moisturized. There are two clipped corners to allow for optimal grip location, so that is a much-appreciated design feature. Nevertheless, the smooth glass edges can make it tricky to get a consistent, sturdy grip. I wear nitrile gloves while using it, so that I feel more confident in the hold I’ve got on it, especially over a hard surface. So, keep that in mind. That being said, though, it is far more aesthetically appealing, user-friendly, and gentler than the traditional pumice stones or foot graters.

A protective storage case would be a great addition to this item. I saved all the packaging and have been placing the file back into the plastic packaging tray and then placing that tray back into the outer plastic packaging box. Something similar to a travel bar soap container or a retainer case would be perfect (slimmer, of course, to fit the file)! The storage case with drainage holes for drying would minimize the risk of breaking the file during cleaning, drying, and storing it. For the current price point, I personally think a reusable storage case should be included.

All that aside, my only real concern, and the reason for the current rating, is that my feet actually felt and looked dryer and rougher several days to a week after the first use. I realize this may be due to my own user error, as I followed the exfoliation with my usual moisturization regimen. It is reasonable to assume I should have taken extra steps to protect and care for me feet immediately following the exfoliation, as the delicate, softer skin was exposed. So, I am going to try it again, this is over-moisturizing and wearing plush socks for the few days afterward. I will update my review with my new results!

Overall, I currently recommend this foot file. I find it to be worth trying out, and is a better alternative to the more abrasive methods. title: Product packaging concerns
text:
The name “Honey Bee Smooth Bath & Body Scrub + Moisturizer” just evokes good thoughts, doesn’t it? If you love honey, it just sounds amazing. I know I love honey and I love using it or having it in my beauty products, so I was looking forward to receiving this product to test it out.

There are some actual product packaging concerns that really should be addressed by the company that makes this body scrub. First off, the jar is pretty sturdy, I’m not going to dispute that and it’s amber, which is always good in helping keep out UV rays. The ONLY seal is the Amazon barcode label (One of the photos shows the label, but I cut through it, it was intact when it arrived - so that was not the issue). There was no shrink wrap seal, neither was there an inner seal, nor one of those inner lid liners. This jar also does not have ANY other labeling except for that Amazon barcode and the top label with their website URL. This was a standalone jar, no box. There is no product information on the jar, no ingredient list, no product name, no manufacture or expiration dates. This brings up heavy red flags for me – quality control especially.

The product description sounds rather amazing, right? Ok, keep in mind what I previously mentioned about quality control. In their description they advertise that you can EAT it. I’d recommend against it because of the lack of quality sealing. It would be one thing if this were given to me by someone who I knew personally that had made the product, but since this is coming from a company that I don’t know and that doesn’t have anything other than the description on Amazon, I’m not sticking this product in my mouth. I know the anti-bacterial properties of honey, however, that doesn’t mean that it can’t be contaminated by anything else -1) it’s not pure honey, there are other ingredients within, 2) who knows the health/sanitation practices of this company, right?, 3) with there just being the barcode label as a seal, who’s to say that someone couldn’t have tampered with it in the warehouse?, and 4) their only label – the one I mentioned with their website URL – if you go to the URL, it comes up with:

“This webpage is not available

ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED”

I don’t know about you, but without anything reputable to back up the product or company, I find it very hard for me to trust this.

ALL of that aside, if you can look past those packaging and trust issues, getting to the actual product…

When you open the cover, it does have that very rich strong scent of honey. The brown sugar and other ingredients have settled to the bottom, so some stirring was necessary — the honey is also pretty solid, so a cosmetic spatula (not included) was not adequate enough to stir it. Once you do stir it, the scent of the brown sugar comes through. Because it’s honey, it’s really sticky, and like any sugar scrub, it has that gritty sugar texture which is great for exfoliation. If your skin is dry when you apply, you may have a tough time spreading it, to avoid this, moisten your skin prior to smoothing this along.

It does its job at exfoliating, removing a layer of dead skin, but I didn’t expect that it wouldn’t. The product itself is good, leaves the skin smooth and smells good – I used it on my leg.

It’s not proprietary though, since there are a ton of DIY tutorials on how to make sugar scrubs out on the web nowadays. But if you’re not into making your own and if they change the packaging and labeling and get a working website up, then this would be the way to go.

I really hope that they get the concerns I mentioned in the beginning straightened out. It would have been a decent product all around if not for those issues. If they do, then I'd be more than happy to bump the rating to a 4. This product was given to me complimentary in exchange for an honest and unbiased review.

title: Without A Doubt The Absolute Biggest Piece Of Crap I've Ever Bought
text:
And that doesn't only go for razors. This thing is the worst purchase of any kind I've ever made in
my entire life. Nearly $200 worth of junk.

I've used nothing but Norelco razors since I was 15 years old. That is well over 25 years now. I've
bought more than 10 different Norelcos over the years. I had not and would not even consider
buying any other brand of razor. Some were better than others, but none even begins to compare
to this piece of junk. The then 10 year old razor I got as a hand-me-down when I was 15 shaved
100 times better than this piece of crap ever did.

I've always bought the top of line Norelco whenever something new and "better" came out. This
piece of crap was no exception. Oh how great they made it look on the commercials all over the
TV. The wonder shaver of shavers, they claimed. Just read the company description here on this
page. It is all lies.

Now I'm not all haired up like a gorilla or anything. I have just normal thickness of hair and
growth. I usually shave every day and with every other Norelco I've ever owned I could get the
job done in less than 3 minutes. Using this hunk of junk it takes well over 15 minutes of rubbing,
scrubbing, and shoving this thing around trying to get it to work. I've tried stretching my skin so
tight that the skin on my neck was pulled up to my earlobe and it still doesn't cut the hair. I've
tried going back and forth, up and down, around in circles, clockwise, counter clockwise,
everything imaginable and no matter how you do it, this piece of junk just does not shave.

Even with brand new blades this razor misses about 1 in 10 hairs on my neck. And when I say it
misses them, I mean it completely misses them. They are not cut at all. It misses about twice as
many under the jaw line. And all of this is after 15+ minutes of shaving! So much for their line of
"even on the neck".

Oh and don't worry, no one will be able to miss that you look like you had a blindfolded 3 year
old give you 10 second shave. I can assure you that after nearly half an hour of ramming and
scrubbing this thing around on your neck, it will have a nice red glow for about 2 or 3 hours that
just screams "hey look at my 15 minute halfass shave". And I do not even have sensitive skin.

If you plan to use the pop up trimmer it is as big of a joke as the rest of the razor. It is about half
an inch wide and while it does work better than the rest of the razor it sounds like a wood chipper
when it is cutting. Think I'm joking? Just get one and try it. The first time I used it I actually
yanked it away from my neck. It didn't pinch or cut me but the sound of it made me think that it
had.

Oh and do not let me forget, you also get the pleasure of stopping and emptying the hair
chambers at least twice during each shave. If you fail to do this it cuts even worse (if such a thing
is possible) because this razor effectively does not have a place to store what hair it does manage
to cut. There are 3 individual hair "chambers" on the razor. One for each cutting head. They fill
up very quickly and then begin to puke the cut hair all over whatever you are standing over while
you are "shaving".

Now after you clean the bathroom sink (or wherever you were) of all the puked hair, you still get
to clean the razor. Don't worry, it is just as easy as running it under the faucet, right? That is what
they claim. Simply running it under the facet works for a few times but that does not get
everything out of the razor and it builds up over the course of a few days.

Now the geniuses that made this piece of junk cleverly decided to make the cutting head all one
piece. Unlike every other Norelco I've ever owned you can not take the cutters out of the combs
and clean them. They are made as all one piece. You cannot even take the cutter and comb out of
the head, everything is all molded together. All you can do is stick the cleaning brush that they
give you (which is as big a piece of junk as the razor) in behind the cutters and try to scrape out
what you can while spinning the cutter around and around. I quickly wore out the the cleaning
brush they supplied and started using a stiff bristle toothbrush instead. That doesn't work very
well either but it is much better than what they give you.

I've tried many different ways of cleaning the heads of this thing and the best way I came up with
was to use a container with a sealable lid and fill it halfway with very hot water. Spray some
cleaner on the head and put it in the container of water and shake it around as hard as you can for
a couple of minutes. I used foaming bathroom cleaner to clean it. Worked well. Might as well use
what you have and with this razor you are going to use a lot of that anyway to clean up all of the
puked hair.

Lastly, if while shaving you are unfortunate enough to get anywhere near to the hair on your head
with this wonder machine, it will suck it up like a Hoover from 3 inches away. Can't cut the hair
on your face and neck to save its life but it will grab hold of your hair from 3 inches away a suck
it into the cutters. Now with the other Norelcos I've had that was never too much of a problem.
You just take the cutter and comb apart and take the stray hair out, but remember this was
designed as a single piece so you do not get to do that. I've spent 5 minutes many times, fishing a
single head hair out of one of the cutters.

So in conclusion, just how bad is this razor?

After a year of all of the above I have just completely had it with the piece junk. And like I said, I've never
owned any other brand of razor, but I feel completely lied to, cheated, and ripped off by this razor
and Norelco. My solution: I have just ordered a Panasonic and I will never again buy anything
made by Norelco. I hope they choke on my money, they will never get another cent of it. EVER!

Avoid the current line of brands unless you use this primarily at home and never intend to drop it!

title: Formidable Competitor to Braun: the Norelco Arcitec
text:
Well, I finally bought one. The Philips Norelco Arcitec 1050. I have been a Braun shaving customer for over 20 years. I find I'm able to get almost as close as a blade. So, why bother with any other shaver? Well, I'd always been fascinated by the triple-head design that Norelco pioneered back almost 30 years ago. The last time I tried one was about 10 years ago, and I wasn't impressed. With the latest Arcitec design, I figured it was time to give it a try.

The Arcitec Models
===================
Philips Norelco makes so many different models, I can't figure them all out. However, the Arcitec stands out by having a very distinctive slender look, the triple head surface on a flat conical piece that is affixed to a pivot, unlike the "neckless" other models. There are 3 main Arcitec models: 1050, 1060, and 1090. There are also two suffixes: X and CC. I think the 'X' means there is no cleaning station, while 'CC' means a cleaning station IS included. You may see some models shown without either suffix--this is the same as the 'X' (before they changed their naming convention). So, why is there a cleaning station if the heads can be rinsed under water? Competition. Braun provides one now... and with the scented alcohol solution, the shaver seems "fresher" after the cleansing bath. So, Norelco had to keep up. But in reality it's overkill; don't bother with one if you're thrifty. Rinsing the heads under water works very well.

Essentially, here's the difference: The 1050 has only 1 indicator for battery recharge needed, the 1060 has several LED indicators showing how much charge is left, and the 1090 has an LED double-digit display showing how many minutes of shaving are left. Quite frankly, the 1050 is just fine. When the battery gets low, you've got about 5 minutes left before the shaver will quit. Even still, for every minute the shaver is plugged in, that is how many minutes of shaving you get. Plug the shaver back in for 5 minutes, and you're ready to go for your shave. So... although this "early warning system" looks cool, it's overkill.

So, onto the shaver...

Appearance and Design
=======================
Out of the box, it is a beautiful looking device. Very futuristic. Adorned in several shades of black, dark gray, and silver, with catchy real carbon fiber side panels and a matte rubber finish along the backside for good grip. The three silver shaving discs contrast the black theme nicely. The shaver is lightweight and the heads have a lot of flex to them. The shaver comes with a charging base that serves as a resting stand, which secures the razor magnetically--very tasteful. There is also a "travel pod" included that allows you to charge the shaver while it is housed inside it. Certainly, the accessories are more impressive than what Braun offers. It looked to me like Braun has met its match.

Then, onto the shave.

The Shaving Experience
========================
This Arcitec 1050 is rather quiet, compared to my Braun 8595 Activator. I watched a couple of YouTube posted reviews of the latest Braun Pulsonic 9595, and that shaver sounded about as loud (if not louder) than my Braun 8595 Activator. So... Norelco certainly wins the prize for most quiet shaver. Actually, the sound is a low drone... it gives the impression that the shaver is a slow, antiquated device. The Braun sounds Bold and Busy with its Bounding Buzz. But in reality, the Norelco is formidable.

So, I touch the shaver to my face. I hear and feel the nibble of whiskers taking place. I begin to go through the motions... cheeks, chin, lip areas, then the neck. It feels comfortable. The discs are gentle. I don't feel anything like the reports of "heavy tugging" at the whiskers. I make a full double-pass across my face, then check the smoothness with my free hand.

Eh... not enough. Still rough. No immediate advantage over the Braun. So, I make another few passes. I pinch and pull at my skin as I would with the Braun. I do two more passes and check the smoothness again.

Eh... not enough. Better, but not as close as the Braun. I continue... I probably ended up shaving about 2-3 minutes longer than with the Braun. I found that after using the shaver for a couple of weeks and getting used to how it works, I'm able to match the Braun in closeness. It just takes a little longer. But the trimmer on the Arcitec? Awful. There's this little ridge on the backside of the shaver. A side switch partially extends and activates it, a small bank of cutting teeth. It's hard to get a nice smooth line. When you encounter a hair with it, there's a rather loud "click" sound. The Braun's trimmer is about twice as wide and zaps the hairs effortlessly. Although the Braun is a louder shaver, the trimmer does not introduce much added noise.

I do notice something else rather positive, though: no whisker dust on my clothes. The Norelco captures the whisker debris inside the heads and keeps it there, unlike the Braun which will dump a bunch of it on you if you turn it sideways or on a downward angle. For people who like to shave after they've gotten dressed, that's good news for Norelco.

Parts Replacement
===================
Norelco recommends replacing the heads every 12 months. Braun recommends doing so every 18 months. The Braun Pulsonic series tells you when head replacement is necessary... not sure how this is done (number of shaves?). The Norelco Arcitec has a little "head replacement" indicator. The Norelco replacement heads are about 30% more expensive than Braun's Series 5, and 8000 series, although the new "cassette" system with the Pulsonic is about the same. So, cost of maintenance might be higher. Also, I've seen mixed opinions about how long they last. Some people have complained having to replace them at 6 months, while an acquaintance says he replaces the heads every 10 years--when he changes shavers! He was once told that the heads are "self sharpening". That sounds a bit unrealistic to me. In any case, I can't report the replacement time here just yet... I'll need to use this shaver for a while. But I'll have to give it to Braun for a longer time between head replacement and at a cheaper cost (because it is also said that you can get away with replacing just the cutter block, if the foil is still intact, which drops the cost by 50%... can't do this with the Norelco).

Conclusion
============
So, the conclusion? The Braun is better overall, but by a slight margin. The Norelco Arcitec 1050 puts up a very good fight. I really could use this razor in place of the Braun, day in and day out. Especially if the girlfriend is still asleep and I want to be super quiet. That's what impresses me the most about the Norelco--it is very quiet. And it is great about trapping the whisker debris (I shave before I get dressed, so it's not a critical factor in my case).

title: Battery looks like it will, but does not readily fit the G290
text:
I have this battery soldered in my old G290 and it is holding a charge like it did when it was first purchased years ago, so if you have a G290, it will work. But here's the problem-the image for this battery matches perfectly the markings on the stock battery in my G290, but the battery shipped is actually about an eight an inch larger in diameter (about same length; has almost no markings). Note that no dimensions are provided for this battery, so it's not possible to determine this in advance. If I didn't fear that I couldn't get the body snapped back again, I'd pull it out and measure it for everyone.

Anyway, here's how to get it to work if you want to revitalize your G290 and you can't find an exact battery match from Norelco or another vendor like I thought I had- to get the body open, take a cheap knife and carefully pry in between the two halves of the plastic body about 2/3s down the body from the top. I applied steadily increasing pressure and the two halves popped apart without damage to the little latches that hold the two halves together (seriously- be careful or you will end up with an open hand instead of an open shaver). Keep the on/off button in the off position! (When you re-assemble the halves, the power button needs to be off to catch a little switch that completes the circuit.)

Look at how the wires run along the side of the battery so you can route them the same way for the new battery. Carefully lift the existing battery up and out of the shaver body, taking care to not break off any of the wires. The wires go straight through the metal tabs on the end of the battery. Touch a soldering iron with a small tip to the underside of the tabs (the side with the wire sticking through) to release the wires- pay attention to which wire goes to the + and - terminals.

Now, pull out a pair of needle-nose pliers, ask your G290's forgiveness, and remove the two plastic ribs on the other half of the shaver (the side that doesn't cradle the motor). You can do this by working the plastic back and forth, gradually tearing off the two ribs all the way down to the shell of the body. If you don't do this, you will not be able to close the two halves together because this battery is larger than the original (the ribs cradled the smaller battery).

Solder the wires onto the correct tabs of the new battery (the tabs are not perforated, so solder the wires flat on the tabs), and carefully place it back into the body so that the wires run along the side, just like they did with the original battery. Now is a good time to find the little switch that gets triggered by the sliding button (the battery has a small charge to allow testing), so make sure the motor runs before you proceed. If not, check the connections and hope and pray that a wire did not break or come loose from a terminal on the switch or charger board at the base of the shaver. If all has gone well, position the two shaver halves, and push them together. They should snap into place. Charge the new battery using the shaver charger for at least 6 hours the first time. I hope it works as well for you...

I've been dying my hair green for about 3 years now. I usually use Pravana, but have been trying out new dyes over the last year or so hoping to find one that didnt bleed as bad. I had high hopes for Arctic Fox, as a lot of people I've talked with swear by it. Sadly, it didnt work well for my hair.

Pros:
-It rinsed SO WELL! The water ran clean within minutes! I was pretty excited. The second wash barely had any dye when I shampooed!
-Super easy to use and put on. The squeeze bottle made it really easy to add additional product to my bowl. Pravana comes in a tube and tends to puncture, so there was no issues there.
-Smelled great
-Didnt stain anything. Not my skin, shower, towels or pillow. The next morning I didnt wake up with green shoulder as I often do after Pravana.

Cons:
-The color pay off sucked. I was hoping for a dark green shade and ended with a vibrant grass green. This didn't bother me much, but I know a lot of people would be pissed by this.
-After the first wash, the color was fading badly to yellow, and has continued to do so.
- I have short hair (chin length), and had to use at least 3 ounces of product to cover my head.

Verdict? I probably wouldn't purchase it again, or recommend it. While I did like that it rinsed out so well and didnt stain, theres no point in using a dye if it doesn't really dye much! Trying Lunar Tides in Juniper next, so hopefully I'll have some better luck there!

Then I washed and blow-dried my hair until it was definitely dry.

He then brushed through each section of hair to make sure that it foamed up like the directions said to.

Right now I have a few streaks of purple and a strange orangey tone left behind on my bleached hair from the Manic Panic.

If you are seeking a personal shaver, go with the Cleancut rather than the Body Bare.

title: Captivating But Concerning
text:
Amore Pacific, based in South Korea, lists "alcohol" as an ingredient in its Color Control Cushion Compact with SPF 50. Since there are good and bad alcohols, I resisted jumping to a negative conclusion especially because I agree with AP regarding the impressive visible benefits conferred by their treatment foundation that has many fans atwitter and aglow.

AP's response to my inquiry was delayed, which I considered either bad (corporate communications) netiquette or bad news. After four workdays, I received a reply thanking me for my "patience" as a response from R&D "to ensure correct information and advice" had not yet been received. When I informed the company that I HAVE no patience and am spoiled by live chats, which provide instant gratification, I received an answer two days later. Apparently, bamboo sap, the primary moisturizing ingredient, is easily contaminated as it's stored for prolonged periods. To prevent "micro-organic pollution," anhydrous alcohol is used. This is ethyl alcohol, which some scientists who write for respected journals warn consumers to avoid because it penetrates the skin barrier and provokes short- and long-term harm, exacerbates oily skin and redness, and may even minimize the efficacy of good ingredients including those that protect against sun damage.

AP is the parent company of Sulwhasoo, which makes a Perfecting Cushion that also includes "alcohol" but not bamboo sap. I don't know what ingredient(s) this brand is protecting.

AP asserts that their anhydrous alcohol is dermatologist approved, but we have no idea who the dermatologist is and whether or not the doctor was paid. AP says that their anhydrous alcohol is patented, but this is just ethyl alcohol with water removed and can't be patented.

The respected Washington, D.C.-based Environmental Working Group (EWG) rates this alcohol a 2 (out of 10) and asserts that anything between 1 and 2 is "low hazard." The overall EWG rating for AP's Color Control Cushion Compact is "4," meaning that it is of *moderate* concern to human health. (The nonprofit group objects most strenuously to the sunscreen octinoxate and to the fragrances included.)

Our U.S. FDA approves the use of ethyl alcohol.

In 2008, the National Institutes of Health urged further investigation, but rigorous double-blind, peer-reviewed studies demand a lot of time and money. Meanwhile, concern lingers.

This is from u/PhDinKava on reddit about this seller, he's made a pretty comprehensive list of Kava vendors to avoid and vendors to go for.
Kava kava is awesome, but there's some sketchy things that occur in the kava realm. One of which is using other parts of the Piper Methysticum (Kava) plant or using a different species altogether. This can be dangerous, and very taxing on the liver. It'll get you krunk, sure, but at what cost?

title: 4.5 Stars - Above Average Performance
text:
After hearing many times of "the fat" I decided to buy my own puck of Mitchell's and see what the fuss was about. It turned out to be a really great soap though not my favorite.

Lather:
Doesn't bloom into a full lather avalanche like TOBS does for me but isn't too thin either. Certainly adequate.

Face Protection:
On the slick side, good blade glide. Just for face protection alone this is a great product.

Cost:
A little on the high side. Razorock has similar soaps available for a third less. I'm not sure that they preform to exactly the same level but since I own some I will be putting this to the test. Not super extravagant though.

Scent:
This is where Mitchell's really loses me. I like strong scents with my shave. TOBS Mr. Taylor is great for a classic yet clean scent that sticks with you. Mitchell's smells like a bar of Ivory Soap. Clean for sure, but nothing to get excited about.

Overall:
I wish I could give Mitchell's 4.5 stars. It will give you a great shave. The price isn't that bad and the lack of strong scent may actually be preferable to some people. If you haven't tried it I suggest giving it a go.

text: Fractionated coconut oil, as the name suggests, is Coconut oil with specific components removed. In the non-chemical fractionating process, the components of whole coconut oil that cause it to be solid at room temperature and be susceptible to oxidation are removed. The resulting substance is liquid at room temperature and very stable. Fractionated Coconut Oil provides a number of advantages over whole coconut oil, primarily increased shelf-life. Unlike whole coconut oil, Fractionated Coconut Oil can withstand light and high heat without going rancid. It is also lighter, non-greasy, and has a greater cleansing effect on the skin, making it popular as a carrier for essential oils and as a base for a variety of skin care products. What I didn't like was the texture of the oil. It was rather thin compared to other beard/hair oils I've used and seemed like it required about twice as much product. I've used two other beard oils on Amazon which I felt were a particularly good value: Gibs, and The Art of Shaving. Both have stronger and more nuanced scent profiles, but both are thicker and have much better moisturizing properties. I'll continue to stick with those.

title: ASP Lightless Gel is awesome for repairing a broken natural nail, a must have!
text:
UPDATE 10/13/14 I had originally rated this item a five stars and I've left my original review unedited because it was accurate HOWEVER I've changed the rating to three stars because of the following.

I've found that when I use this product to repair a broken, or pealing or split nail, when its freshly applied, it's awesome BUT when a few days go by and the product starts to get old it starts to lift and the problem is that even being very careful, if the product peals from the nail, IT TAKES A FEW LAYERS OF THE NATURAL NAIL WITH IT and that's what I was one of the things I was trying to prevent when I applied this product...What I ended up doing was soaking off the remainder of this product and patching the now really damaged area of my nail with ASP Fiberglass
http://www.amazon.com/s/ref=nb_sb_ss_i_0_6?url=search-alias%3Daps&field-keywords=asp%20fiberglass&sprefix=ASP+fi%2Caps%2C272 and two layers of brush on nail glue which is the method I plan to continue using from now on since it does not lift and tear my nails...http://www.amazon.com/Spilo-MISC-Bondini-Plus-Brush-On/dp/B0002Z8SE8/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&qid=1413205777&sr=8-1&keywords=brush+on+nail+glue.

Although I bought mine at my local Sally's, this product is so awesome, I had to come an give it a thumbs up!

Now let me say that I have natural nails that tend to break at the base (bead) of the nail & so cutting them is not a painfree option nor a pretty one at that ;)

The only reason why I use all three products (listed below) is to repair broken nails, to give them time to grow out while I get to have pretty, all the same length nails ;)

This "light less gel" has a thicker consistency than brush on glue, which by the way, was the method I was using prior to coming across this gem in a YouTube tutorial video.

Now it does not come with a brush applicator so I took an empty nail polish bottle, cleaned it out & I filled it with pure acetone to prevent the brush from getting hard; & that's the brush I use to apply this gel. Just make sure to wipe the brush a few time on a napkin before using to wipe off the acetone.

After I've removed the old nail polish, I wipe my nail clean with either an alcohol pad or some acetone. I then cut an appropriate piece of the fiberglass to cover the break. I apply the fiberglass to the clean nail & I apply a thin line of this gel over the patch, then I take my handy, dandy nail polish brush & I spread out a thin layer of the gel over the entire nail, same as if I was applying nail polish. Then I spray the Gel Cure (which is a god sent because it dries this thick gel almost instantly) & voila! the nail is as good as not, well you know ;) Now depending on the size of the break, use your judgement to determine if you need a 2nd layer. This method last more than the regular nail glue & as such, soaking it off will take a little more time but who cares as long as your nail has time to grown without suffering from either pain or an odd looking manicure ;)

When you add the cost of the fiberglass, the gel & the cure, you are looking at approximately $30 BUT this will last a long, long, long time so for me its cost effective.

If you have natural nails that tend to split, these items are a must. These are staples in my "manicure rescue arsenal".

Highly recommended items for sure!

I have used Sonicare toothbrushes for years. I have had great dental visit reports because of using the brush twice a day and flossing once. title: Pure retro red
text:
When everyone was wearing clear or neutral glosses, I wasn't phased. I'm a red lipstick addict from way back, and I just toned down the red and added a little gloss to update it.

Thank God, though, it looks like real, pure reds are making a comeback. I read about Besame's vintage cosmetics line, and as my MAC red was about gone, I figured I'd try one of their reds.

My coloring is a brunette with a very fair complexion. Frankly, except for goth dark reds, I can wear pretty much any shade. I picked Besame Red since it seemed middle of the line in terms of color, and I wanted to get an idea how this cosmetics line worked.

The first thing that surprised me is it comes on a card. This lipstick isn't cheap; you'd think the packaging would be a little nicer. (I get they're trying to do vintage cosmetics, but if you're going to make it look like Coty or Max Factor from the 40s, you probably don't want to charge a hefty price for it.)

The other surprise is that the tube isn't heavy. Everyone raves about the metal container, but like so? It's lightweight. I've had some heavy lipstick containers from luxury lines that bragged about the lipstick containers being jewel-like, and they were.

This container isn't.

So now with my quibbles out of the way, let me say the lipstick itself is NICE. Some said the lipstick is small; it isn't. It seems about the size of most lipsticks with a double bevel to make putting it on easy.

I always use a lipbrush (does away with lipliner and makes lipstick in the case last FOREVER. You'll get tired of the lipstick before it runs out.)

The first surprise is the scent. I don't recall any lipstick except some glosses having a discernable scent. This one does, rather vanilla-y. It's pleasant.

The lipstick texture in the tube is, surprisingly, moist. It goes on easily, but it's not so moisturizing that the color doesn't last.

I put it on and did the old fashioned lip blotting with a piece of toilet paper. With a super slushy lipstick, this will almost take the entire thing off. Not so with Besame. The color is very saturated and stayed on my lips nicely.

The lip blotting didn't get rid of the moisture. My lips still feel nice. The color lightened up a bit (which happens with blotting.) You're supposed to add another layer of lipstick after this, but I usually don't. The color was still very saturated, so there was no need for more.

The staying power is excellent! It lasted all day, and my lips never dried out.

If you love the color (and use a lipbrush), you'll get WAY more out of this true red to the point where you'll get tired of it before it runs out.

I'm definitely going to be investigating more of the Besame line.

N.B. One other trick that works if you want your lipstick to last into next week. Blot the first coat and put on a bit of powder with your finger - baby powder or compact powder does nicely. Blot again, and put on another coat of lipstick. It'll last through dinner and into next Christmas. :)

title: Useful for Travel, but Too Many Shortcomings for Everyday
text:
The Philips Norelco 8040X electric shaver is a compact, lightweight unit that can be used dry or wet. In either case, it uses Nivea for Men shaving conditioner to smooth the razor over your face as you shave. Ultimately, it is capable of delivering a good shave, but it has too many drawbacks to recommend for everyday use.

SHAVING PERFORMANCE

Used dry, the 8040X is below average compared to other shavers that I've used (including my five-year-old Norelco which still shaves rings around this one). Its shaving heads are very compact and pivot nicely so you can easily reach all contours of your face and hard-to-reach areas, e.g. under your nose. However, the blades themselves don't do provide a close shave at all. I have a beard that's only moderately thick/stiff, and the 8040X left me feeling like I would have a five-o'clock shadow in minutes.

Used wet in the shower, its performance is much better. This is also when the Cool Skin moisturizer really shines - in fact, it's downright necessary to get the heads to glide over your face when used wet. It has a pleasant scent and does leave the skin on your face feeling refreshed afterward (even if it's also apparent that the "cool" is just from some alcohol in the formula). It certainly won't be the quickest shave that you've ever had, but if you take your time, you can get results that rival even a blade.

USE & MAINTENANCE

The 8040X comes with a cradle for storing it upright and also for charging it. Unfortunately once the razor becomes fully charged, you can't leave it in the cradle without unplugging it - doing so can damage battery life. Plus, the plug for the cradle is gigantic and ugly, so you won't want to leave the cradle on display anyway. I would have preferred a simple direct-cord charge design instead.

The Nivea conditioner that is used with the shaver is expensive in the long run - about $6 for a can that will last about a month (don't believe what the box says - it's only a month's worth). Suddenly that close, wet shave is looking pretty pricey in terms of time and money compared to simply going back to shaving with a blade. Also, the pump system that feeds the conditioner into the razor is proprietary, i.e. you can't just fill it with any skin conditioner because only the Nivea Cool Skin fits the razor's plug. So, you're out of luck if you don't like the scent or feel of the Nivea product. Also, the razor would lose just about all usefulness if/when they stop making those cans.

There is no readout to display the remaining battery life. Instead, the power light will begin to flash when the battery is getting low. Given the cost of this razor, this seems like a cut corner. I don't like the idea of guessing how much juice I have left.

The razor needs to be cleaned after each shave. Compared to most closed-head designs, this makes for even more time that the razor requires with each use. You also need to regularly check that the tubes which deliver the moisturizer haven't become clogged.

It does have a travel lock feature which will prevent the razor from accidentally turning on while you have it packed away. Coupled with its compact size, I think that the "weekend getaway (not for business)" may be the ideal application of this razor.

CONCLUSION

The 8040X Moisturizing Shave System promises too much. Ultimately, it works best when shaving wet, using a lot of the moisturizer, and taking a lot of time to do so. This, coupled with its lightweight, compact design, good battery life and travel lock make it ideal for weekend getaways. But given its cost - both immediate and in the long run - this just isn't enough return on your investment.

PROS
* Close, comfortable shave when used wet
* Compact and lightweight
* Travel lock prevents accidents while razor is packed
* Good battery life

CONS
* Unimpressive shave results when used dry
* Expensive cost-to-operate due to (very necessary) moisturizer
* Demanding upkeep/maintenance requirements
* Lack of battery gauge

I bought the "Vanilla Rainbow Sprinkles" fragrance on another website, as a substitute for Bath & Body Works' "Confetti Cake Pop", which had been sold out everywhere that I had looked online. I was under the impression that the two scents would be similar enough so as to not make much of a difference. I was, unfortunately, very wrong.

"Confetti Cake Pop" is awesome, and it smells just like what the packaging says, "creamy cake frosting." Delicious! "Vanilla Rainbow Sprinkles", on the other hand, is one of the few Bath & Body Works' scents that I heartily dislike. For one thing, the vanilla scent is very muted; not in a good way, as in subtle, but in a bad way, like "I can barely notice the vanilla in this perfume." If that was the only thing about "Vanilla Rainbow Sprinkles" that was off, I could live with it.

After I had sprayed it on myself, however, I became aware that there was a strong under-note of alcohol. I do not wish to smell like rubbing alcohol when I put on scent. Just awful. That bottle will be going into the trash can, and I will not buy "Vanilla Rainbow Sprinkles" in the "mist" (or in any other B&BW product) ever again. It is disappointing, as I usually have good luck with Bath & Body Works, and I enjoy many of their fragrances. I have to also comment that, unusually for Bath & Body Works, the artwork on the product label is very dull and is rather uninspiring.

Looking for a sweet, fun scent that is good enough to eat? Instead of "Vanilla Rainbow Sprinkles", I would recommend Bath & Body Works' "Sugared Snickerdoodle", if you cannot find "Confetti Cake Pop".

The first time I opened the bottle to smell this stuff, I have to say I was really disappointed. I found it to be overly strong and perfumy. But what I've found is that the aroma DOES tone down quite a bit, both during and after the shave, and turns into something a bit more subtle. Still strong-ish, but more curious now than offensive. I find myself rechecking to see whether I've decided yet whether I like the smell or not. I think that in a more dilute form, I do actually like it. Go figure.

As for the shaving experience... After a proper prep -- face wash, hot water rinse, rubbing about a dime size drop of oil into my face and neck, waiting 2 minutes, then whipping up some WSP sandalwood/black vanille -- I went about shaving with my trusty DE and a very aggressive Feather blade. First pass (WTG) was smooth and without issue. Relathered for a second pass (XTG) and found the experience equally slick and comfortable. No nicks, smooth shave, and the combined scent of the oil and the WSP soap was a winner.

Bottom line: It's different, and most definitely not for everyone or every shave even. But it does what it claims to do, and it does it well. Considering the vast range in unit prices of shaving products out there, this is fairly reasonable. I may very well decide to cut it with some castor/argan oil to tone down the scent a bit, but I do consider it a keeper now. Cancelled my return, glad I showed a little patience.
