title: Pleasant Enough, Not Much Scent, Need a Lot of Product To Shower
text:
Like all too many organic soaps, this example ends up being a bit too subtle and bland in scent and power to justify its price point. I love vetiver but even with a generous dollop on the loofah, I get only the faintest scent of that fragrance here. The hemp / vetiver combo smells pleasant in a mild sort of way, but this is not what I expected at the price point and given the product name. If I wanted "fragrance free", I'd buy it!

Besides the really mild non-especially vetiverish scent, NH IH&V body wash also needs a lot of soap to generate any lather, and even needs a lot just to get through a whole body wash. Lather may or may not be to your liking, but having to reload the loofah halfway through your shower is no one's idea of fun. At the rate of product usage, I would be amazed if this 13 oz bottle lasts me for more than 2-3 weeks.

Ultimately, even if you want to stay organic, there are better choices with more prominent scents and better product consumption rates. EOs Cedar & Mint for Men works well enough and can even be used as a shampoo and shave cream for the undemanding. My personal favorite semi-organic products are from Every Man Jack. Their cedar and sandalwood (two separate types there) body wash have great smells and give adequate lather and cleaning duration with roughly half the product needed to get similar effects from NH IH&V wash. (I call Every Man Jack semi-organic as I haven't bothered to assess all the ingredients on their label, but they have no parabens or SLS derivatives, so they pass my personal screening standard.) Both of these product lines are much cheaper than Nubian Heritage.

For vetiver lovers who want that scent in their bath ritual, Provence Sante makes a good vetiver beauty bar soap, and also a rather expensive vetiver body wash. which I have not tried due to its high cost. I have tried the beauty bar, and though not cheap, it does indeed give the user a noticeable vetiver smell when applied, which is always a good thing when buying a vetiver named product!

title: Hard pressed, don’t pick much up, not very pigmented. Wish they provided more photos to choose color
text:
This claims to be titanium dioxide free, gluten free, made with natural and organic ingredients, vegan, and free of parabens, nano-particles, bismuth oxychloride, talc, silicones, mineral oil, GMOs, artificial fragrance, artificial preservatives, FD&C dyes, carmine, and phthalates. It is made in the USA. The ingredient list is on the product box and it is really short (see photos). It claims to be formulated with natural ingredients, such as Kaolin Clay and Jojoba Oil. They say they are cruelty free. The product page has a photo that says “Leaping Bunny Certified,” but the logo on the box is a PETA logo. I checked both websites and HYNT Beauty is certified by both Leaping Bunny and PETA.

I got the shade “Linen Kiss.” A little searching online showed it was a matte ivory. I really didn’t like they didn’t have much info at all about the shades to choose from. There weren’t any descriptions of the different shades to say whether they were matte, shimmer, etc. There weren’t photos other than the product in the little singles compact. I would have liked to have seen more product photos, like swatches comparing the different shades to help me choose, or at least a description of each shade. I had to search on Google and even when I went to their website there were only 4 shade options there. At least there they had a description for the 4 shades, but they only had the single photo of each in the singles compact. For a single eyeshadow coating $22, I expect more. The focus on the ingredients and what isn’t included is good, but they should also put a little attention on providing customers with more photos so they can easily pick a shade that’s right for them and be happy when the get it. Not have to guess what finish it has or if they shade is going to look like it does in the pan when they get it.

This comes in a little ziplock bag. Inside is a little outer product box.

It comes in a plastic singles compact. The top flips open easily.

It’s a matte ivory.

I show a photo where I swatched it. I did a finger swatch on my clean forearm (no lotion, primer, etc.). I swirled my finger in the pan and it seemed really hard pressed, like I wasn’t picking up much. I looked at my finger to see what I had picked up and should have been surprised after how much I swirled it in the pan that I didn’t have more, but I wasn’t really because of how hard pressed it felt. I took a photo showing it on my finger. As you can see, it isn’t very opaque and doesn’t look like I picked much up. I swirled a lot and that’s all I got. I swiped that onto my forearm. Then I went back into the pan. This time I pressed harder into the pan while I swirled. I picked up the same amount and put a second layer over the first one I had already done. Then, I did the same thing and did a different swipe. I did 3 layers for that one to show how it built up. It showed up enough on my fair skin, but I wasn’t a fan with how hard pressed this was. Maybe if I didn’t get such a light shade I’d like it more? But, I feel like the formula just isn’t too great and wouldn’t have great pigmentation with any color.

It’s nice and smooth.

Overall, its okay. It’s not for me. For me to spend $22 for a single eyeshadow, the eyeshadow needs to be pretty darn good. This just isn’t it. It’s too hard pressed for my liking. You don’t pick up much product and even when you do it doesn’t have that much pigmentation. Like I said, maybe with a different color it would be different, but I don’t think so. There’s way better options out there. I don’t recommend this.

title: Not bad, but not great either
text:
I bought this because I needed something to store my lipsticks in. I do like that each row has its own level, making it easier for me to see where each lipstick is, at a glance. Because it has a square (rather than rounded) base, this box sits on my desk and is flush against the wall, making organization easier (personal preference).

I'm just a little disappointed that the plastic seems to be quite thin and brittle, because the reviews I read indicated that the plastic is sturdy. I think for the price I could have easily went elsewhere to get a makeup organizer that is made up of a more substantial plastic. I'm reminded of the material that is used for CD and cassette cases when I hold this item in my hand. My case had a few hairline cracks near the bottom edge corners; maybe this is due to shipping? (It came packaged with a thin layer of cardstock wrapped around it)

This is also due to preference, but looking at how angular this box is (compared to other cosmetic organizers that have rounded edges) I thought I would like it, but when I look closely I see that the edges look to be unfinished, and they scrape the lipstick cases if they happen to touch the edge as I remove/replace them into the little slots. I fixed this by putting tiny amounts of liquid cement (for acrylic) on the edges so that they smoothed over, but I wish I didn't have to do this extra step.

Overall I will still use this product because it suits its purpose, but in the future I will be more wary of product details.

title: Works great to hold lashes with a thick enough line!
text:
First of all, I want to make it clear this is LINER GLUE - an eyeliner and lash glue in one. You get a clear one and a black one. Both are liner glue. I wanted to make that clear because I saw another review that said something about only expecting the tube with white liquid to be the glue and how it was stickier than the liner. I’m not sure what tube with white liquid the reviewer is talking about. Maybe the clear pen? Maybe this product page once had another product and the review is for that, which happens sometimes. I’m not sure. I just want to make it clear that BOTH the clear and black pens are eyeliner AND glue in 1.

They actually claim this is a 3-in-1 product - Eyeliner, lash glue, and eyelash serum. So, it claims you can use both pens as an eyeliner. You can use both pens as lash glue. And both pens are lash serums.

It wasn’t too long ago that I found out about 2-in-1 liner and glue pens. When I first found out about them, I thought they would be a gimmick and wouldn’t work, but they do...but not always. Like with any product, some work better than others. This one works well.

The caps - on the one hand they are on good and snug and won’t slip off, but on the other hand they are a pain to get off! You have to tug so hard that when it finally comes off you end up swiping the pen on your hand. That’s a pain! I’m hoping with time after removing the cap it’ll become looser and not so hard to remove!

The liner works well. The black is pigmented. It’s a little runny so it can bleed/feather. It stays put well. The clear is clear so I didn’t really try it as just a liner. If you’re using it just as a liner, it has a stickiness until it dries down completely, which doesn’t take long. If I’m just going to reach for eyeliner and not use false lashes, I wouldn’t really reach for this. I have liners I prefer over this one. It works nicely as the liner with your false lashes. I just wouldn’t really recommend it if you’re not going to use it with false lashes.

The glue part works well. If you shake it really well first, apply it immediately, apply a regular thickness line, and immediately apply your lash, the liner will hold your lashes really well and hold them all day. I say regular thickness line because with my small, hooded eyes, I tightline so my line is extremely thin. But, if you don’t tightline and do a regular line, the glue will hold well. But, if your line is too thin, the lashes will lift. If your eyes water at all, the lash will lift in that area. Luckily, you get a clear and a black one. The clear works well for me because I can do a thicker line and it dries clear so I don’t mind it! Unfortunately, the black one isn’t for me. This shaver is a bit of a disappointment. Based on the price and the reviews, I was expecting a really GREAT shaver. I give it three stars for "mediocre." It's just OK, definitely not great.

I can't even use the trimmer on the same charge as shaving. The bigggest disappointment is the EXTREMELY short duration of motor run time per full charge.

Shaving: It takes a LONG time to shave your face with this thing. Combined with the short motor run time per charge, that's a real issue. If you have a lot of time and you really enjoy shaving, I guess you might not mind how long it takes. I'm usually in a hurry. It takes approximately 50% longer to shave my face with this shaver than it did with my old Braun.

The gel dispenser is kind of a novelty item. I usually pump the gel out onto my fingertips and spread it on my face that way because it's too time consuming and uncomfortable to spread it with the shaver. When I use up the gel that came with it, I'll probably just use something else after that. Don't buy it based on the gel pump. It's no biggie.

The pros of this thing are a very COMFORTABLE and QUIET shave, albeit time consuming.

Quality of Shave: The closeness of the shave is AS GOOD any electric shaver I've owned, but not appreciably any BETTER. Definitely not as close as a blade, but hopefully no one is THAT naive!

Trimmer: The trimmer angle is good. Actually, I like the trimmer other than the fact that I can't trim on the same charge as shaving.

I'll probably keep using this thing since I've already bought it. But if I had it to do over again, I'd choose something else.

title: Use it right and it'll work great
text:
I actually like this straightener brush. I had read mixed reviews on them because I've been wanting to try one so I've been researching different brands and reading reviews. This works really well but you have to work with it. You cant just brush it through your hair and expect great results. Thats not how it works. And that's not how any typical flat iron works so I dont agree with people thinking this should be any different. It has it's pros and cons but more pros than cons. I tried this on my straight yet frizzy hair. And I tried this on my daughters curly hair. I had good results with both.

Pros: It came quickly in the mail and was nicely packaged
It appears to be made with good quality
It heats up fast and the numbers on the screen climb up as it heats so you can tell what temp it's at while you wait
It doesnt burn you and all of the heating units are well covered for your protection
It glides nicely through your hair
It makes your hair soft
Works better on frizz than a flat iron
Easier to use than a flat iron
Helps maintain volume

Cons:
It's only in Celsius
If heated all the way to the highest temp it stinks
The cord is kinda short
At times it pulls your hair out

Now if you use it right it will work really well for you. What I did initially was comb it through the hair like a brush. I had combed my hair with a bore bristle brush before doing this. It kinda sets the hair up for you to section well. I sectioned the hair and held it straight up and put the straightening brush right up to the scalp and combed under and out creating an arch with it so that my hair would curl under. I was able to straighten more hair at once with this than a normal flat iron. All I did to finish my hair was to keep sectioning hair and using the same motion by going on the under side of the hair and arching out I created a really nice looking style. My hair had less frizz, was softer, had more volume and more bounce to it than when I've used a flat iron. So I guess I'll be using this from now on. My only concern was the smell that happened when turned all the way up but I've had other irons that smelled too. So I'm assuming it's the silicon or rubber caps to protect your head. You dont need it turned up all the way. I was able to create the style I wanted at the half way mark.
I'll keep using this and if I have any problems I will update this post.

title: Works ok, but a wet/dry trimmer is the way to go!
text:
Had this trimmer for 2 years and it died last week after sliding into the bathroom sink under running water....

While it was working it was a good trimmer overall, though I really didn't like have to switch out the trimmer heads for the standard and then the detail sized cutters--on more than one occasion I was in a hurry and fumbling around looking for the other cutter assembly than what was on the trimmer. Another issue was that it was relatively easy to move the height adjustment by accident when taking off and replacing the plastic trimmer guard, which you need to do in order to switch cutting heads. It wasn't a really big deal, but a lot of times I wouldn't remember which number I had the hair length set on, and then I would have to guess what setting I had it one the last time I used it.....The vacuum feature was nice I guess in that it doesn't get too many little beard trimmings all over the sink, but then again it's really easy to just turn on the sink and rinse it, or, use the trimmer over a rug where you'll never see the small trimmings.....

But the big lesson here is to be sure buy a wet/dry beard trimmer that won't die if it gets a little wet. I just bought the Panasonic ER224S All-in-One Cordless Hair and Beard Trimmer [[ASIN:B000F4USF8 Panasonic ER224S All-in-One Cordless Hair and Beard Trimmer (Silver)]] which was almost half the price of the Phillips Norelco unit and it's a wet/dry trimmer that you can use in the shower. It also has a built-in detail trimmer so you don't have to switch cutter heads and worry about loosing attachments. Unfortunately, I can not recommend this product, as it did not work for me.

PROS:
- Unscented
- Its Natural/Aluminum-free Deodorant (As a former Peace Corps volunteer who completed my 27-month commitment, I really appreciate natural alternatives)

Recommendations:
- Release a version for MEN (in my Ron Swanson voice)
- Eliminate the wooden stick, release a rolling stick version

Disclaimer:
I live in NYC and walk 1/2 block to the metro, 4 blocks to the office and back, five days a week...

Update 3/17: I have been buying these nails since Oct 2020, and I have absolutely loved them, unfortunately this recent batch I got has been awful. They break so easily; I shut a door and they break, I wash my hands and they break. I mean like, the nail breaks in pieces, leaving sharp edges and half the nail stuck to my real nail. It’s awful. This used to happen here and there with these nails, but it’s happened with every manicure I’ve done with this recent batch.
I also noticed my nail polish isn’t applying as smoothly over these nails, and it’s taking forever to dry. (Tried and true nail polish that doesn’t apply this way usually). Something about this plastic has changed significantly. I’m super disappointed.

October 2020: This is going to be a long, informative review! First, my needs, in case what I was looking for is different from you:

I wanted medium length fake nails to paint over. I work in retail and am obviously washing/sanitizing my hands constantly, so my nails are refusing to grow. I don’t like getting my nails done either. So these for me are perfect and meet all of my needs. The negatives and positives in general are laid out below!

Negatives:

-The reviews saying you can see the pixels in the whites of the nails are correct. However, it’s so unnoticeable. I don’t think you should worry about that. Unless you’re a hand model, nobody will notice teeny tiny pixels on the whites of these nails.
-You can see the glue underneath. This isn’t a problem for me because I paint over them anyway. Also, again, I doubt anyone would notice that either. It’s obvious when you look directly at the nails and analyze them. But who realllly can get close enough to you right now to do that?
-Three of these nails have broken, like split down the middle. This is over the course of like 4 or 5 manicures though, so not bad.
-They pop off easily. This could be the glue (Kiss). I like this about them though. I just keep my glue in my purse with me. I don’t want to ruin my nail bed, and sometimes I’ll apply a nail wonky and I count on it popping off so I can fix it haha.

Positives:

-The shape
-The length
-The variety
-The texture

It took a few tries to get down which sizes worked best for my nails (I have wee hands. I am a small person. The attached pic of me and my partner don’t exactly show that. I’ve seen one complaint being that these are too small, but idk how that could happen because there are literally so many sizes ¯\_(ツ)_/¯). I use the Kiss glue which works in 5 seconds, then file the tops a little bit, apply my nails polish without a base coat (it sticks better to these smooth nails). I also apply the fake nails to my non dominant hand first. Trust me on that one. You can see how they improved with each look I did. Was still figuring myself out for the pink manicure.

Anyway, I love these and will definitely repurchase! Several people asked if I was getting my nails done professionally. Plus, my nail beds are totally fine! They are actually stronger since these protect them from all of the stuff I do at work. Highly recommend and will repurchase when I finally run out.

text:
When I started growing my beard, I already had a good moisturizing face wash and was surreptitiously "borrowing" some of my g/f's hair conditioner (the kind you put in after shampooing, leave in for a couple minutes, then rinse out), which worked reasonably well to soften my beard. I wanted to upgrade to a beard-oriented product to keep the softness and help tame fly-aways (and avoid my g/f's ire), so I decided to try this, along with adding a beard brush. As a face wash/shampoo, it's fine -- it cleans well and the smell is light and neutral (pleasantly reminds me of the old-school barbershop that cut my hair when I was a kid). However, I was very disappointed by the conditioning (or lack thereof). Even after two weeks of use, my beard just wasn't as soft, and I had more fly-aways than before. I tried washing and rinsing, as well as leaving it in for a couple of minutes before rinsing, and found no difference. As a test, I used the other conditioner again after this, and softness returned, which suggests this product doesn't have sufficient quantities of the "conditioning" ingredients and is really more of a 2-in-1 face wash/shampoo.

Ultimately I wanted to like this, but I found I get the same results with my normal (not-beard-oriented) moisturizing face wash + beard brush, as I do with this product + beard brush, at less than half the price. So, if you need beard conditioning, look elsewhere, or plan to add another product at additional cost (I now see this brand makes a separate beard moisturizer / leave-in conditioner product.)

However, if you don't currently have any sort of face wash and suffer from "beardruff" or itching, this will probably help you, albeit at a premium price. Side note, the packaging is good and thoughtfully includes both a pump-type and a flip-up cap to accommodate your shower or travel preferences.

title: I Wanted It To Work!  Didn't Work on My Gel Nail Polish
text:
Made in China, this nail polish remover kit is just so cute and complete! I really really wanted it to work.

I love my gel colors. I use them on natural nails.

I HATE removing the gel colors! I HATE what it does to my natural nails.

It's a quandary.

So, this Gel Nail Polish kit said it would remove the polish in 5 minutes.

It comes with a 16.9 oz bottle of remover (which is alcohol, acetone, propylene glycol, essence, deionized water. I usually just use straight acetone and that doesn't always do the trick, but okay.
A little pump bottle to put the remover in. You just put the pad on the top and pump a couple of times to saturate the pad. I LOVE those little pumps! Sooooo much better than trying to saturate the pads by dumping the bottle upside down on top of the pad and having it all over the place!
A huge bundle of cotton pads.
10 finger tip clips to hold the pads on--love!
Nail File
Metal cuticle pusher/scraper.

I was wearing Pewete nail gel from base coat to top coat. There was 2 coats of glitter nail polish and some nail stickers. I know it was a tough test.

To give it the best possible chance, I used my nail drill and scuffed the top coat off of my nail. You can see it after being scuffed in the 6th picture.

Then, I wet a cotton pad and put it on the nail and put the clip over it.

And waited.

Checked.

Waited.

Checked.

Waited.

This went on every 5 minutes for about 15 minutes and by that time the little cotton pad was pretty dry.

I finally just took the clip off and it looked like the second to the last picture so I used the metal cuticle pusher/scraper to scrape the polish off and ended up with the one in the last picture. I finally just used my normal gel polish remover to take the last bit off.

So, this kit is nice but it just didn't work like my normal gel polish remover which works in just a few minutes and doesn't beat up my nails or skin.

I think this kit would work with regular nail polish fine, but it simply can't cut through the gel. At least the gel that I used. I think all of the alcohol and other chemicals that diluted the acetone just made it too weak.

Would not recommend for gel nail polish removal but it would work on regular nail polish I believe so it got 3 stars for that possibility.

title: Too Hot to Touch
text:
Upon opening the box, I assumed I was getting a steal of a deal with how fancy the box looked. Then, there was a box within that box that looked just as nice. I was very impressed by the packaging. The box included the hair dyer, two different end caps, and a piece of paper with description, instructions, warranty info, etc.

The instructions didn’t really give much useful information. Nowhere on the piece of paper did it mention why you would choose to use one head attachment over the other. The biggest confusion was having no description as to what the buttons on the hair dryer were for. The images on the instructions did not match what was on the hair dryer. (See picture of the buttons – the two larger buttons both have the same symbols with no description)

I put one of the head attachments on the hair dryer, then plugged the unit in. It immediately started running, so I had to use the trial and error method of figuring out which button controlled the speed and which button controlled the heat. The hair dryer had a good weight to it and wasn’t difficult to continually hold up to dry my hair. I’ve got medium length, fine/thin hair, and it took a little over 6 minutes to fully dry my hair. While using the hair dryer, and especially after turning it off, the black end attachment was extremely hot to the touch.

Comparing to a Revlon hair dryer of the same wattage, they are almost identical in size. When using the same hot/high dry setting, the Revlon hair dryer only took about 4 ½ minutes to dry my hair. Not a huge difference, but worth mentioning. They both have around the same loudness while running. The most important difference between the two hair dryers was the temperature of the end cap attachments after using to dry my hair. The Revlon hair dryer’s end cap was 143F after I finished drying my hair, while the xtava peony hair dryer’s end cap was 256F!

Overall, this hair dryer is just okay. It’s a good basic hair dryer, but I don’t know that I would pick it to use every day. The generic buttons on the machine and lack of instructions on what they were for was annoying, but obviously could be figured out after one use. I’m more disappointed in how dangerously hot the end piece gets after using it for just a few minutes of use. I typically have to switch positions of hair tools in my hands when I’m drying my right side vs my left side, but with how hot that end piece gets, it’s not practical to touch it to rotate it. I would hate for my toddler to get ahold of it after I use it and hurt himself (yes, you’re supposed to keep it out of reach of kids, but anyone with young kids knows how fast their little hands start feeling around on the counters as far as they can reach). If you don’t have young kids and have a high heat tolerance, the temperature of the unit while/after using likely wouldn’t be an issue, but for me, it’s a deal breaker.

title: my friend bought this and recommended it. I must say I love it
text:
my friend bought this and recommended it. I must say I love it. Hyaluronic works because :
I have a new skincare obsession: hyaluronic acid. I’ve been using hyaluronic acid for about a month and I’m amazed at what it’s done for my acne-prone skin. Inspired to learn more about how the stuff works (and if it’s really ok to put something involving the word “acid” on your face), I talked to a few experts to find out what hyaluronic acid is and why, exactly, it’s so awesome.

I first read about this magical stuff called hyaluronic acid over on I Heart Daily (tons of good stuff over there, all the time, by the way!). Then I found it recommended over and over again as an ingredient in facial creams in the beauty magazines I read on a recent flight. So I thought, why not try it? I ordered up a bottle and started using it, twice a day.

And whoa. When I layer this on underneath my regular daily moisturizer with SPF, my skin looks incredibly dewy. Yup, dewy. I’d always read that word in beauty mags but thought it was just an overused editorial cliché, not a descriptor that could ever be applied to my own skin, with its large pores and tendency towards oiliness. But dewy it was. And the acne that’s plagued me since 7th grade (over half of my life) has considerably lessened, too. All of a sudden, I have beautiful, clear, perfectly moisturized skin, even in the dead of winter.

I’m pretty committed to being as “natural” as possible with my skincare, meaning I try to buy products that use ingredients sourced from nature rather than chemicals and plasticizers. I knew I loved hyaluronic acid, but I wanted to know more about what it actually was and if it fell into my own admittedly loose category of “natural.” (Yes, I know I probably should have done more research before I started slathering it all over my face.) Here’s what I found out:
What Is Hyaluronic Acid?

Hyaluronic acid isn’t necessarily a new ingredient in skincare, but it’s been growing in popularity in recent years. According to Dr. Jessica Krant, dermatologist, founder of Art of Dermatology and Assistant Clinical Professor of Dermatology at SUNY Downstate Medical Center:

Hyaluronic acid, or hyaluronan, is the body’s lubricant molecule. It is basically a very big and complex sugar-related molecule called a glycosaminoglycan that is found naturally throughout the body and works in many different ways to keep us healthy and active. It’s involved in the health and function of skin, joints, and the immune system, among others. It is very popular as used in a number of cosmetic fillers known as hyaluronic acid dermal fillers, which get injected under the surface of the skin to replace lost volume and fill deep folds. Lately, topical products have begun to include the molecule as a moisturizing or antiaging ingredient.

So, it’s found naturally in the body and is commonly used in fillers. Ok. But if it’s found in the body, where, exactly, does the hyaluronic acid that I use on my face come from? Cosmetic dermatologist Dr. Oscar Hevia explained that cosmetic hyaluronic acid is made in a lab:

The current method of production involves bacterial fermentation, a process whereby genetically modified bacteria can produce the hyaluronic acid in large quantities which is then filtered extensively to obtain a purified, finished product.

Is Hyaluronic Acid Natural?

So is something that’s made in a lab “natural?” Dr. Hevia continued:

…it depends how you define “natural.” Most would probably not utilize this term for a substance that is produced by genetically modified bacteria, but nonetheless, the finished product is pure and identical to human hyaluronic acid.

For what it's worth, the instructions just have us dabbing a couple dots on with the sponge and blending with the fingers or brush. The sponge is an entirely unnecessary addition.

As you can see from the photo, this did allow me to put a nice and thick layer on my arm just in case anyone is looking to see how dramatic it can be. I do like the color, it's a good match, but I wouldn't use it on my eyes or my lips because the product says 'liquid blush.' There is a graphic on this page that says 2-in-1, despite showing eyes/blush/lips on the very same graphic, which I am pretty sure would be 3-in-1.

The last issue is the ingredients. The top ingredient is Ethylhexyl Palmitate, which is a pretty well known comedogenic (pore clogging) problem, so it's not great if you have breakouts. That's why I don't know how long it lasts or well it holds up over time, it's not worth the high risk of breakouts so I didn't wear it long. You might have guessed that 'palmitate' is also a derivative of Palm Oil, which is an industry that is destroying many biodiverse forests.

Two stars for color, texture feels nice, but I would only recommend this to people with clear skin that don't really have any desire to use the applicator sponge.

title: Pros and Cons to Consider
text:
I have very dense, thick, and long 4C hair, so my texture is the most coarse texture of hair to possibly test the durability of this blower-dryer comb. Anyone that has coarse or thick hair such as yours truly, likely runs into the same problem as me when you blow dry your hair after a washing. The dang blow-dryer comb keeps popping off and/or the teeth bends and snaps off. So annoying! Since this is very expensive for a blow-dryer comb, I'm sure ladies will appreciate this critical review before purchasing. Here are the pros and cons I've come across.

Pros...The material is the highest grade of plastic (not at all rubber) I have seen in a blow-dryer comb. It appears to be equivalent to the "plastic" material cooking utensils are made of, so the teeth does not easily bend/break. The finer and less dense your hair is, the longer the life-time you will have this comb. If you attach it securely, the comb actually works without popping off.

Cons...This seems to only work for dryers with a narrow barrel, and not so much for the dryers that has a bubble shape. It will pop off dryers with a bubble shaped barrel, because it will be impossible to secure it on a nozzle tip that is not cylinder-shaped. All you need is a phillips screwdriver to attach it. Since I have 4C hair, I did actually notice slight bending of a couple teeth, and the bending increased after a 3rd usage. After my 3rd hair drying, I tried to hand-bend the teeth back in place, and 2 snapped off! $40 bucks (cost and shipping) down the drain :-( Also, what you don't know until you see it in person is that there is a metal bar inside the comb, that is being raked against your hair as you are combing it, which will eventually cause heat damage with prolonged usage, especially if you dry your hair on high.

My overall assessment is that, yes it worked better that expected. Although 2 teeth broke on mine and others slightly bent, I plan on buying another one to have on-hand, as I currently have not come across any better options. But, I'm going to take a break from this comb for a while, and try drying my hair with a paddle brush and my dryer because the thought of that metal bar inside the Willie Morrow comb, raking against my hair with every usage is alarming, and will surely heat damage my hair.

title: Perfect little filigree cuffs
text:
These Dreadlock Beads for Hair, Braids and Locs caught my eye. I actually wanted them for two reasons. One reason being that summer is coming and I wanted to do a slightly BOHO look with little braids without having rubber bands showing. I LOVE summer BOHO and silver filigree is just my style so these beads (which are actually more like cuffs) are perfect for me. The second reason I wanted these is that I am starting to make handmade dolls and these would be perfect for a little boho doll I am currently working through the design on. I found several good things about these little beads:

-they are lightweight so they won't weigh heavily on your hair and damage it
-they are easily opened so that you can slide your hair in and not have to 'thread' it through
-they are not large (only 8mm) or overly ornate so they add to your hair design rather than take away from it
-they can be used at the root of your hair, the middle of your hair or the end and are still comfortable to sleep on
-they come in a pack of 50 which is more than ample for your hair styles (although if you have very thick hair and are using two per braid or dread you may want to get more)
-they lock onto your hair or braid snugly

The only downside I had with these little cuffs was when I used the first one. It was my fault though as I closed it too quickly and a bit too hard, I flattened the poor little thing. Unfortunately once you flatten them they are near impossible to get round again. The next one was simpler. I had opened it gently, slid my hair through and placed my thumb and forefinger on either side of the opening and GENTLY pushed the ends back together and VOILA! perfectly round still! With each bead it got easier and easier until I didn't even think about it anymore. To get them over a rubber band simply slide your braid into the bead then slide it down over the rubber band rather than trying to open and close it enough to fit the rubber band. Also wrap the rubber band in such that it is the same length and the bead (or a little shorter) so that there is no 'belly' and it is hidden by the bead.

Overall I found these little beads to be just what I needed! I did get my first pack at a discount in exchange for a fair review and that is what I have done. I LOVE these little beads and am looking forward to getting more for myself and my creations.

text:
I ordered this wig in 10 inch, 180 density. I’ve had it for a little over 6 weeks. I cut mine more equal in the back, so it was more like a bob.

Pros
Very good quality hair. I’ve washed it a bunch, colored it three times (more on that further down), styled it with heat many, many times, and even slept in it a few times. It always goes right back to looking new.

The size of the cap is, in my opinion, perfect. It is big head friendly and long enough to go over the sideburn area in front of the ears. I’ve never owned a wig that fits me this well.

There’s basically no shedding, and it doesn’t have any matting or areas that tangle.

Very well executed ombré.

Pretty long life. I wear this a lot.

Cons
This wig is not cute out of the box. The curl that came in mine was honestly ugly. Thankfully it is not permanent. After the hair is washed and dried, it has a very nice slight natural wave.

This is not necessarily a con for me, but the lighter section is definitely brassy. I wanted mine orangey red, so this was a good starting point for me.

This wig does not dye well and the color will be mostly gone within a few washes.

The hair is not evenly distributed. I’d say the back half is 100% density, maybe 130. The hair on the lace is like no joke 400% density. There is so much hair on the lace. I’ve plucked and plucked and plucked and there’s no improvement. So the hair in the front is puffy because there’s so much hair. This wouldn’t even be entirely bad except that a lot of the hair on the lace is only 2-3 inches long so the thickness doesn’t follow through all the way down.

This is the biggest con. One of clips on the adjustable strap came broken, and I didn’t realize until I had started customizing it. Lesson learned there. I’m fine with doing some work on my wigs, so it’s not a huge deal. But someone else may not be comfortable doing so.

I give it three stars due to the weird hair distribution and broken clip. I would probably buy this wig again when this one dies. However, I would definitely recommend not paying extra for more density.

title: Cheap Plastic Wind-Up Toy Masquerading As An Epilator
text:
I have been a long-time user of Emjoi epilators. In fact, I've only ever used Emjoi epilators because they worked well for me. So, when my last one died recently, I was excited to see this model touting 60 tweezers instead of the measly 36 tweezers on my old Emjoi. I am not an especially hairy person, but I love how epilating makes my legs, arms, and underarms so much smoother than shaving. The main drawback is that it takes longer to epilate because the head is usually so small and you have to repeatedly go over the same area to make sure you get all the hair out. I was hoping that having almost twice as many tweezers working would make the job go faster. Apparently, I was wrong in that assumption.

The first thing that struck me with the eRase was the size. It is tiny! (See my pictures comparing it to my old Emjoi Soft Caress) I have medium-sized hands, and the eRase is a slippery little bugger to hold onto for an extended period of time. It doesn't help that the whole unit is made of smooth plastic with no bumpy or grippy parts to help your grip. I ended up having to sort of pinch it with my fingertips the whole time I used it. Very ergonomically bad for your hands.

The other main thing that I noticed was that the whole thing - other than the tweezers - seems to be made of plastic. You can see in my pictures that even the gears that drive the tweezer heads are plastic. I can't imagine this epilator lasts long with plastic gears. It's really no better than a little high-powered wind-up toy (it even kind of sounds like one when it's running).

As for the hair removal part - the whole reason why I would buy an epilator - it was mediocre at best. It did not save me any time over my 36-tweezer model. The eRase is so tiny that it didn't cover any more surface area, and the design is flawed so that the two heads seem to get in the way of each other and actually pull out less hair per pass than my old model. I also felt like it was just ripping the top part of the hairs rather than removing them from the roots. I noticed, too, that it did not remove the fine hairs on my underarms and legs very well at all. Also, for the very first time in my 20+ years of epilating, I got some of my underarm skin caught between the tweezer head and the back of the unit. Ouch! I'm still feeling the effects of that 2 days later.

There are other small details that made decide to return this epilator. The fact that it's corded was what I wanted. The cord, however, is not attached, so over time, it can become loose with constant plugging/unplugging (That's what happened to my last epilator). Since it needs to be plugged in for it to work, it would be better if the cord were attached to the epilator. I also don't always have a problem with things made in China - I buy them with the full knowledge that I most likely will get what I pay for - but this cheap, plastic, epilator is worth less than the $60 I paid for it.

Things I didn't do with this epilator:

- Epilate my face or private areas. I don't do that, so I can't tell you how well this epilator works for those areas.
- Use the sensitive skin attachment. I'm used to epilating, so the tiny, prickly feelings don't bother me anymore.

Overall, I was sad to have to return this epilator (assuming the vendor will take it back) since I had such high hopes for it. I guess I need to start looking for a different brand...?

Edit on 10/21/16: I was able to return this epilator, but because it wasn't sold by Amazon, I had to pay return shipping. The return shipping costed me about $7, so I basically paid $7 to try this epilator. Definitely not worth it since I could have bought a different, slightly more expensive epilator sold by Amazon, and returned it for free. So, keep this in mind if you buy something that is not being sold by Amazon - there may be free shipping to get the item, but you will pay to return it if you don't like it!

title: It works, but you have to be careful where you use it.
text:
My experience with this stuff is a little humorous. The first thing to note is the instructions are under the barcode sticker. A second thing to note is that even though this stuff is supposedly made in the US, the English on the bottle is not the clearest.

I followed the instructions and soaked my feet first. To make things a little easier, I went ahead and used a shaver on some of the larger calluses. Then, I went in with the callus remover. My bright idea was to sit on the edge of the tub and do it so I could just easily wash everything off when I was done. I waited a few minutes and started scrubbing and sure enough, everything easily came off and my feet were left super smooth.

Now comes the part I wasn't anticipating. This stuff makes surfaces slick; skin, bathtub, I'm talking everything. This stuff also doesn't wash off very easily. I ran and ran and ran water into the tub and kept washing and washing and washing and it was like being covered in Dawn Detergent that refused to come off. So with everything being as slick as it was, I couldn't stand up for fear of falling. After about 10 minutes, I have to be honest, I started to panic. title: My favorite natural fragrance lotion: No Sensitivity problems for me!
text:
It does smell like an orange creamsicle in the best way (yummy!), but if I get a big direct sniff of my hand right after putting it on, it does have the smell reminiscent of eating a really good tangy, fresh apricot, too.

Even some lotions that advertise “natural fragrance,” I have sensitivity to, but this one is no problem! No sneezing, wheezing, or headaches from it. It’s a delicious smell, but not too strong or overpowering, and not fake smelling. The scent subsides quickly after a short bit of time passes, but is still there if you sniff the skin directly. I’ve tried their lavender & lemon coconut (both tend to be favorite scents/scent combos for me when done naturally), and those are nice, but this is my favorite one, unexpectedly.

I normally make my own really moisture intensive thick creams & lotion bars (with beeswax, cocoa butter, shea butter & olive oil.) These I usually apply to my hands every time I wash, because my skin dries out so easily. It keeps cracked hands at bay. This lotion is not a replacement for intensive creams like that.

But this lotion is lovely when I want something that *doesn’t leave my hands feeling greasy*, applies easily, soaks in nicely, & smells good. It’s kinda my “treat myself” lotion. I can also put it out for guests who are used to more traditional lotion consistency, and have them like it, while not being a problem for my breathing. It works great to include in a gift basket, too.

I can’t say this will work for every person with scent sensitivities (and don’t assume it’s okay if someone’s told you no scents...some people have dangerous health reactions to even natural fragrances, among other possible serious concerns that need to be respected), but it is definitely one worth looking into if you are the one with sensitivities, trying to find scents you are okay with. It is 1000 x better than most of the lotions with synthetic fragrances, and even some of the stronger ones that claim natural fragrance.

title: Overall great razor
text:
This is my first new razor in several years, so it's basically being compared to a 7+ year-old Norelco. Also, I have never shaved using traditional blades, so I can't compare it with that experience. With this said...

Pros: There's a lot I like about this razor. It gives a really close shave. Much closer than I've gotten from previous electrics. It still could be a little closer, though, but not by much. It's cordless, which is very convenient, and the charge seems to last quite a long time. So far, one charge seems to last about 4 weeks for me, with shaving every day for about 3 minutes or so. Pretty good. It also is very ergonomically designed -- very comfortable to hold. I like that it is so quick to charge -- only takes about one hour. You also have the option of cleaning it with either water, or with an included brush. The water does a great job of cleaning out all the little hairs. I still worry about getting it wet too frequently, though, so I usually clean it with the brush and just clean it with water about once a month.

Cons: The biggest con is that while there are "charging" and "done charging" LEDs on the razor, there is no "Battery Low" LED. This means you only know when the battery is dead when it dies while you are shaving. Once you've gone though a couple charge cycles you will learn about how long it goes between charges, but nonetheless it'd be nice to have a warning. It's really only because of this that I knocked off one star. But one other con is that the power adapter is somewhat large, as opposed to older Norelcos, so if you choose to use it as a corded razor, it might be inconvenient to store the adapter near the razor if you keep in, for example, a medicine cabinet.

Other thoughts: Worth noting that you don't need to use the included stand if you don't want to -- the cord can plug directly into the razor for charging. Also, it can operate as either a cordless or corded razor, although the manual warns that using it as a corded razor too often will hurt the battery, so you pretty much have to choose one or the other. Comes with a very small travel pouch, head protector, and brush. Great razor overall. Only knocked it one star because there's no Battery Empty LED... some other Norelcos have this feature, but many of them are more expensive than this one. This is a great value for the money.
